## Overview
**AAF-McQuay** refers to the company created in **1994** when **SnyderGeneral Corp.** was renamed and reorganized into two principal operating businesses: **AAF International** and **McQuay International**. In practice today, the domain provided (**aafintl.com**) represents **AAF International**, the air-filtration business. AAF traces its roots to **1921**, when engineer **Bill Reed** developed an air filter for his automotive paint shop; Reed Air Filter later merged with seven manufacturers to form **American Air Filter (AAF)**. AAF is headquartered in **Louisville, Kentucky**.

AAF is a **manufacturer of air filtration and clean-air systems** serving commercial, industrial, residential, cleanroom, energy, and critical-process applications. The company states it operates in **22 countries** and supports customers in **more than 100 countries**.

## Products & Services
AAF’s portfolio centers on **air filtration equipment and clean-air solutions**. Key categories include:
- **HVAC equipment and filtration**
- **High-purity HEPA/ULPA equipment and filtration**
- **Gas-phase filtration**
- **Commercial, industrial, and residential air filters**
- **Industrial dust collection and air pollution control**
- **Energy filtration equipment** and replacement filters/parts
- **Services and monitoring solutions** for indoor air quality and filtration performance

Historically, the McQuay side of AAF-McQuay focused on **commercial HVAC equipment**, including chillers, air handlers, and related systems, though the McQuay business was later absorbed into Daikin’s applied HVAC operations.

## Scale
- **Estimated revenue:** **$706.1M** (user-provided)
- **Employee count:** Apollo estimates about **1,100** employees for AAF International; historically, AAF reported **more than 3,000 employees** worldwide around the 2016 Flanders acquisition.
- **Geographic footprint:** **22 countries**; support presence in **100+ countries**
- **Locations:** **22** (user-provided / consistent with company footprint statements)
- **Headquarters:** **Louisville, Kentucky, U.S.**

## Market Position
AAF describes itself as a **global leader in air filtration**. Reputable historical sources described AAF International as the **world’s largest manufacturer and marketer of air filtration products and systems** in the 1990s. In **2016**, AAF’s acquisition of **Flanders** was positioned by both AAF and parent **Daikin** as moving the company to the **#1 position in the global air filtration market**, particularly strengthening its North American presence and high-purity/cleanroom offering.

## History
- **1921:** Bill Reed founds Reed Air Filter; foundation of AAF
- **1920s:** American Air Filter formed through merger of Reed Air Filter with seven other manufacturers
- **1984:** SnyderGeneral acquires **McQuay Inc.**
- **1988:** SnyderGeneral acquires **American Air Filter**
- **1994:** SnyderGeneral is acquired by interests linked to **Hong Leong/O.Y.L. Industries** and renamed **AAF-McQuay Incorporated**
- **2006:** **Daikin** acquires O.Y.L./McQuay; AAF becomes part of the Daikin Group
- **2016:** AAF acquires and merges with **Flanders**, expanding cleanroom and HEPA capabilities
- **2021:** AAF marks **100 years** in business

Today, AAF remains the filtration-focused part of that legacy, operating as a longstanding **clean-air and filtration manufacturer** within the broader **Daikin** group.

## Overview
**Actuant** is the former name of **Enerpac Tool Group Corp.**, a public industrial manufacturer focused on **high-pressure hydraulic tools, controlled force products, and heavy-load positioning solutions**. The company was **founded in 1910** and historically was headquartered in **Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin**; in **2025** it relocated its headquarters to **Milwaukee, Wisconsin**. Enerpac Tool Group trades on the **NYSE under the ticker EPAC**.

The company serves industrial customers in **more than 100 countries**, supporting mission-critical and often hazardous applications across end markets such as infrastructure, power generation, general industrial, refining, mining, and maintenance/repair operations.

## Products & Services
Enerpac Tool Group designs, manufactures, and distributes industrial tools and related services. Its portfolio includes:
- **Hydraulic cylinders, jacks, pumps, and power units**
- **Torque and tension tools**
- **Heavy lifting technology** such as gantries, strand jacks, and positioning systems
- **Portable machining and flange maintenance tools**
- **Workholding, cutters, pullers, punches, and system components**
- **Service, rental, and joint integrity solutions**

Key brands highlighted by the company include:
- **Enerpac**
- **Hydratight**
- **Simplex**
- **Larzep**

## Scale
- **Revenue:** **$616.9M** in fiscal **2025** (company reported **$617M** net sales)
- **Employees:** approximately **2,000-2,200 globally**
- **Geographic reach:** serves customers in **100+ countries**
- **Locations:** company materials indicate a broad global footprint across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia, and Australia; user-provided data lists **42 locations**
- **Distribution:** approximately **800 distributors** globally (FY2025 annual report)
- **Market cap:** about **$2.2B** (Apollo / FY2025 annual report references)

## Market Position
Enerpac Tool Group describes itself as a **premier industrial tools and services company** and a global leader in:
- **High-pressure hydraulic tools**
- **Controlled force products**
- **Solutions for precise lifting, lowering, and positioning of heavy loads**

The company has increasingly positioned itself as a **pure-play industrial tools and solutions provider** following portfolio simplification and the 2019 rebrand from Actuant to Enerpac Tool Group. In FY2025, it reported **record revenue since the relaunch of Enerpac Tool Group in 2019** and an **adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.9%**, indicating strong profitability relative to many industrial peers.

## History
- **1910:** Founded in Wisconsin; roots trace to **American Grinder and Manufacturing**.
- **1920s-1950s:** Expanded into hydraulic technology; the **Enerpac** brand emerged from the industrial products business.
- **2001:** Company adopted the **Actuant Corporation** name.
- **2019:** Announced rebrand from **Actuant** to **Enerpac Tool Group** as it focused on becoming a pure-play industrial tools and services company; began trading as **EPAC**.
- **2021:** **Paul Sternlieb** became President and CEO.
- **2024:** Acquired **DTA The Smart Move**, expanding its heavy lifting technology capabilities.
- **2025:** Moved headquarters to downtown **Milwaukee** and opened an expanded innovation-focused headquarters space.

Overall, Actuant/Enerpac Tool Group is a long-established U.S. manufacturer with a specialized position in fluid power and industrial tooling, combining branded products, engineered solutions, and service capabilities for demanding industrial applications.

## Overview
**Acument Global Technologies** is a privately held manufacturer of mechanical fastening and assembly solutions for industrial markets. The company operates as a **Fontana Gruppo** business and is headquartered at **6125 E. 18 Mile Rd, Sterling Heights, Michigan 48314**. Acument traces its current identity to **2006**, when **Textron Fastening Systems** was established as a standalone company under the Acument brand after acquisition by **Platinum Equity**. Its legacy brands and predecessor businesses date back to the **1950s and 1960s**.

The company serves a broad set of end markets including **automotive, aerospace, industrial, building & construction, commercial truck, construction equipment, defense, and electric vehicles**.

## Products & Services
Acument designs and manufactures a wide range of fastening products, from standard catalog parts to engineered application-specific components. Core offerings include:
- **Bolts and screws**
- **Nuts**
- **Washers**
- **Assemblies**
- **Ball studs / tie rods**
- **Thread-forming fasteners**
- **Engineered specials**
- **Clinch products**
- **Double-ended studs**
- **Fluid fasteners**
- **Plugs**
- **Drive systems**

The company is especially known for established proprietary and branded fastening technologies such as **Camcar®**, **Ring Screw®**, **TORX®**, **TORX PLUS®**, **STRUX®**, and **Mag-Form®**. In addition to manufacturing, Acument offers **application engineering, testing, design support, inventory/logistics support, and supply-chain services**.

## Scale
Available scale indicators suggest a mid-sized North American manufacturing platform with global reach:
- **Revenue:** approximately **$543.1M**
- **Locations:** **10** manufacturing and distribution facilities across North America
- **Employees:** commonly cited at **more than 1,500**; third-party sources and database records often place the workforce around **1,700-2,000**
- **Headquarters phone:** **+1 586-997-5600**

Some sources also note additional **logistics/VMI centers** and **R&D locations** supporting operations.

## Market Position
Acument describes itself as **one of the world’s leading mechanical fastening producers**. Its products are used by major OEMs and industrial manufacturers, with cited customers including **Ford, General Motors, Stellantis/Chrysler, Volkswagen, Magna, Boeing, Honda, Airbus, Caterpillar, Whirlpool, and ZF Group**. Its market position is strengthened by long-established brands, engineering capability, and a diversified customer base across transportation and industrial sectors.

## History
- **1950s-1960s:** Legacy businesses such as **Camcar** and **Ring Screw** were developed.
- **Over time:** These operations were combined under **Textron Fastening Systems**.
- **2006:** **Platinum Equity** acquired Textron Fastening Systems from Textron and created the standalone **Acument** brand.
- **2008-2009:** The company underwent restructuring during the global automotive downturn.
- **2014:** **Fontana Gruppo** acquired Acument from Platinum Equity.
- **2024:** Acument and Fontana Gruppo marked **10 years together** under Fontana ownership.

Overall, Acument Global Technologies is a long-established fastener manufacturer with deep roots in transportation and industrial fastening, backed by proprietary brands and North American manufacturing scale.

## Overview
**Allied Building Products Corp.** is a U.S. **building materials distributor** focused on exterior and interior products for residential and commercial construction. The company was **founded in 1950** in **Jersey City, New Jersey** as a family-operated roofing and custom sheet metal fabrication business. Its headquarters has been in **East Rutherford, New Jersey**.

Allied became one of the larger specialty distributors in its category, serving contractors and other professional customers nationwide. Prior to its acquisition, it operated under **CRH plc / Oldcastle** ownership for more than 20 years.

## Products & Services
Allied distributed a broad portfolio of building materials, with a strong emphasis on both **exterior** and **interior** product categories.

**Exterior products included:**
- Roofing materials
- Siding and soffits
- Windows and doors
- Waterproofing products
- Tools and accessories
- Insulation and related products

**Interior products included:**
- Wallboard / drywall and accessories
- Suspended ceiling systems
- Acoustical ceiling tile and accessories
- Insulation and related interior construction materials

The company positioned itself around product availability, delivery capability, and contractor-focused service programs.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$2.56 billion** (user-provided)
- **Locations:** **208** branches/locations
- **Geographic footprint:** **31 U.S. states** before acquisition
- **Employees:** more than **3,500** employees cited around 2017-2018; third-party databases also estimate lower current counts reflecting post-acquisition integration
- **Fleet:** more than **2,785 vehicles** cited in Beacon acquisition materials
- **Headquarters:** East Rutherford, New Jersey

At the time Beacon Roofing Supply announced its acquisition, Allied was described as operating **coast to coast** and as one of the country’s largest exterior and interior building products distributors.

## Market Position
Allied held a strong position in U.S. specialty distribution for building materials, particularly in roofing and interior products. Beacon described Allied as **“one of the country’s largest exterior and interior building products distributors.”** The acquisition also highlighted Allied’s importance in the **interior market**, where the combined company became the **fourth-largest wallboard and acoustical ceiling tile wholesale distributor in the U.S.**

Its scale, broad branch network, and product mix made it a meaningful player in markets such as the **Northeast, New York/New Jersey, and the Upper Midwest**.

## History
- **1950:** Founded in Jersey City, NJ as a family-run roofing and custom sheet metal business.
- **1996:** Acquired by **CRH plc** for about **$121 million**, according to Reuters.
- **2000s-2010s:** Expanded through organic growth and acquisitions, broadening from roofing into siding, windows, doors, wallboard, ceilings, insulation, and related categories.
- **August 2017:** **Beacon Roofing Supply** announced an agreement to acquire Allied from CRH for **$2.625 billion in cash**.
- **January 2018:** Beacon completed the acquisition, after which Allied became part of **Beacon Building Products**.

Overall, Allied Building Products evolved from a regional family business into a large national distributor with substantial reach in professional building materials supply.

- **Gear drives and gear motors**

## Overview
**Ambu A/S** is a Danish **medical technology manufacturer** focused on single-use endoscopy, anaesthesia, patient monitoring, and diagnostic solutions. The company was **founded in 1937** by engineer **Holger Hesse** (originally as Testa Laboratory) and is headquartered at **Baltorpbakken 13, 2750 Ballerup, Denmark**. Ambu is publicly traded on **Nasdaq Copenhagen** under **AMBU-B**.

Ambu’s stated mission is to develop products that **save lives and improve patient care**. It is best known historically for the **Ambu Bag**, the world’s first self-inflating resuscitator, launched in **1956**.

## Products & Services
Ambu’s portfolio spans three broad areas:

- **Single-use endoscopy**: bronchoscopes, video laryngoscopes, rhinolaryngoscopes, duodenoscopes, gastroscopes, cystoscopes, and ureteroscopes, plus display and processing units
- **Anaesthesia & airway management**: resuscitators, breathing bags, laryngeal masks, face masks, double- and single-lumen tubes, and endobronchial blockers
- **Patient monitoring & diagnostics**: ECG electrodes, EEG/EMG electrodes, intraoperative monitoring products, and related diagnostic devices
- **Emergency care & training**: cervical collars, ALS/BLS training manikins, simulators, and related training products

A major strategic focus is **single-use endoscopy**, where Ambu offers products across the four major segments: **pulmonology, ENT, urology, and gastroenterology**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$875.7M** (user-provided)
- **Employees:** about **5,000-5,200** globally
- **Geographic footprint:** workforce in **20+ countries**, serving **60+ markets**
- **Locations:** **21** (user-provided)
- **Manufacturing footprint:** production sites in the **U.S., Mexico, Malaysia, and China**
- **Largest market:** **North America**, representing **more than 50% of annual revenue**

Ambu says its products help more than **100 million patients annually**.

## Market Position
Ambu positions itself as a **global leader in single-use endoscopy**. Company materials state it holds **more than 60% market share** in single-use endoscopy and offers one of the market’s most comprehensive product portfolios. Its differentiation centers on infection control, workflow efficiency, immediate device availability, and avoiding reprocessing and repair requirements associated with reusable scopes.

The company also emphasizes sustainability innovation, including the **first endoscope handle using bioplastics** and its **Ambu Recircle** take-back and recycling program.

## History
- **1937:** Founded by **Holger Hesse** as Testa Laboratory
- **1956:** Launch of the **Ambu Bag**, a landmark in emergency care
- **1960s-1970s:** Expanded internationally through distribution and sales companies; added training and resuscitation products
- **1986:** Renamed **Ambu International**
- **1992:** Listed on the stock exchange, marking its transition to a more international public company
- **2001:** Acquired **Medicotest**, becoming a major European electrodes manufacturer and strengthening patient monitoring
- **2009:** Launched the world’s first **single-use flexible bronchoscope** (**Ambu aScope**), a pivotal step in its current growth strategy
- **2018-2020:** Expanded single-use endoscopy into **ENT, urology, and GI**
- **2024-2025:** Introduced bioplastics-based endoscope designs and a recycling program, reinforcing its sustainability agenda

The company is headquartered in **Tarrytown, New York** (660 White Plains Rd) and describes itself as a global masterbatch leader. Ampacet develops formulations that improve the **color, appearance, processing, durability, and sustainability** of plastic products.

Its solutions are used across a wide range of end markets, including **packaging, consumer goods, appliances, automotive, health care, 3D printing, aerospace, agriculture, infrastructure, and industrial products**.

Ampacet’s portfolio centers on **masterbatch products** and related technical support:
- **Color masterbatches**
- **Black and white masterbatches**
- **Special effects masterbatches**
- **Functional additive masterbatches**
- **Process aids** and processing solutions
- **Custom color development** and color-matching
- **Technical, analytical, prototyping, and on-site troubleshooting services**

The company also offers sustainability-oriented solutions designed to help customers **reduce waste and energy use, incorporate post-consumer resin, and improve recyclability**.

- **Headquarters:** Tarrytown, New York, U.S.
- **Employees:** about **2,000+**

- **Countries with operations:** **17**

## Overview
**Apergy Corporation** was a U.S.-based oilfield equipment and technology manufacturer focused on helping customers **drill for and produce oil and gas safely and efficiently**. The company was **incorporated in October 2017** as Wellsite Corporation, **renamed Apergy in February 2018**, and became an **independent public company on May 9, 2018** through a spin-off from **Dover Corporation**. Its headquarters were in **The Woodlands, Texas**.

Apergy operated across the well lifecycle—from **drilling and completion to production**—with a portfolio centered on engineered hardware, automation, and digital oilfield technologies.

## Products & Services
Apergy reported two main business segments:

- **Production & Automation Technologies**
  - Artificial lift systems and equipment
  - **Rod pumping systems**
  - **Electric submersible pump (ESP) systems**
  - **Progressive cavity pumps and drive systems**
  - **Plunger lifts**
  - Automation, software, and **IIoT** solutions for:
    - downhole monitoring
    - wellsite productivity enhancement
    - asset integrity management

- **Drilling Technologies**
  - **Polycrystalline diamond cutters and bearings** used in drilling applications

Its brand portfolio and acquired businesses included names such as **Harbison-Fischer, Norris, PCS Ferguson, Norriseal-Wellmark, Quartzdyne, Windrock, Spirit, Accelerated, and US Synthetic**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** roughly **$1.1 billion-$1.2 billion** prior to the 2020 merger
- **Employees:** more than **3,000 associates globally** at the time of the 2018 spin-off
- **Geographic footprint:** operations in **8 countries** as a stand-alone company; later, the planned combined company with ChampionX was described as operating in **55+ countries**
- **Headquarters:** **2445 Technology Forest Blvd, The Woodlands, TX 77381**
- **Ticker:** traded on the **NYSE under APY** after the spin-off

## Market Position
Apergy positioned itself as a **leading provider of highly engineered equipment and technologies** for the upstream oil and gas market. Its strengths were in **artificial lift, production automation, digital monitoring, and drilling components**, with a particular emphasis on productivity and production optimization. The company also highlighted an industry heritage of **more than 60 years** through its predecessor businesses and acquired brands.

In late **2019**, Apergy announced a combination with **Ecolab’s upstream energy business (ChampionX)** to form a broader **production-optimization** company. Management described the transaction as creating a global leader with complementary positions in **artificial lift, digital technologies, and production chemistry**.

## History
- **Dec. 2017:** Dover approved the plan to spin off its upstream oil and gas business.
- **Oct. 10, 2017:** Wellsite Corporation was incorporated in Delaware.
- **Feb. 2, 2018:** Wellsite Corporation was renamed **Apergy Corporation**.

## Overview
**Apria Healthcare** is a U.S. provider and distributor of home healthcare equipment, supplies, and related clinical services. The company focuses on helping patients receive care at home, especially in respiratory therapy, sleep apnea treatment, wound care, and pharmacy support. Apria was **formed in 1995** through the combination of **Abbey Healthcare Group Inc.** and **Homedco Group Inc.** Some data providers trace legacy roots to **1924**, but the current Apria organization dates to 1995.  

Apria’s current headquarters is listed in **Indianapolis, Indiana** (7353 Company Dr), while older corporate references also point to **Lake Forest, California**. The company serves patients nationwide across the continental U.S. and Hawaii.

## Products & Services
Apria provides home-based medical equipment and support across several core categories:
- **Respiratory care:** oxygen therapy, non-invasive ventilation, nebulized respiratory medication, and COPD-focused programs
- **Sleep care:** CPAP and bi-level PAP devices, masks, supplies, coaching, and resupply programs for obstructive sleep apnea
- **Wound care:** negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) equipment and supplies
- **Pharmacy:** respiratory-focused homecare pharmacy services and medication support
- **Home medical equipment:** rental and purchase of equipment for in-home care, plus patient education, delivery, setup, and ongoing support

The company also operates consumer-facing channels such as **ApriaDirect** / **ApriaHome** and offers provider-oriented support and insurance claim handling.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$1.145 billion** (user-provided; company materials have also cited **over $1 billion** in annual revenue)
- **Locations:** about **280 branch locations** in the United States
- **Employees:** roughly **6,100-6,500 employees** based on Apollo, PitchBook, and company statements
- **Patients served:** approximately **1.8 million to 2 million patients annually**
- **HQ phone:** **+1 888-492-7742**

## Market Position
Apria describes itself as a **leading national provider** of home healthcare equipment and services. Its scale, large branch footprint, extensive Medicare experience, and broad payor network support that position. Company materials state it is among the **largest home healthcare providers in the U.S.** in its categories, particularly in respiratory and sleep-related home care.

Comparable companies mentioned across market sources include **Lincare, Rotech Healthcare, AdaptHealth,** and other home medical equipment providers.

## History
- **1995:** Apria was created through the merger of **Abbey Healthcare** and **Homedco**.
- Over time, the company expanded through acquisitions, including businesses such as **Medox (2005)**, **Coram (2007)**, **Praxair Healthcare Services’ U.S. homecare business (2011)**, and **ABC Health Care (2021)**.
- Apria has highlighted more than **25 years of continuous accreditation** by **The Joint Commission**, and has said it was the first company of its type to obtain voluntary accreditation from that body.
- Ownership changed over time: Apria was previously public, later private under **Blackstone** ownership, and more recently became part of **Owens & Minor** through its home healthcare platform.

Overall, Apria is a large, established national player in home-based respiratory, sleep, and durable medical equipment distribution and support.

## Overview
**Aramsco** is a private **specialty distributor** serving contractors and facility maintenance professionals across the **U.S. and Canada**. The company supplies mission-critical **equipment, chemicals, consumables, tools, and safety products** used in restoration, abatement, environmental services, surface preparation, professional cleaning, janitorial/sanitation, traffic safety, and stone care.

Aramsco was **founded in 1966** as a regional supplier of industrial safety products. Official company materials describe its headquarters as **Paulsboro, New Jersey**; some business databases also reference **Radnor, Pennsylvania** as a corporate address. The company phone is **+1 800-767-6933**.

## Products & Services
Aramsco sells a large catalog of specialty contractor supplies, with sources citing **more than 40,000 products** and some investor materials citing **over 45,000 products**. Its portfolio includes:

- **Restoration and remediation** supplies for fire, water, mold, asbestos, lead, and hazardous-material cleanup
- **Concrete and steel surface preparation** equipment and consumables
- **Professional cleaning, janitorial, and sanitation** products
- **Traffic safety** and related jobsite products
- **Stone fabrication and stone care** solutions
- **Facility maintenance** products

In addition to distribution, Aramsco offers value-added services such as:
- **Training and education**
- **Equipment rentals**
- **Equipment repair**
- **Equipment financing**
- **Technical support before, during, and after the sale**

## Scale
Aramsco operates a broad North American footprint. Company and investor sources indicate **over 70 locations across North America**, while more recent investor and ratings sources cite **more than 80 branches/distribution centers**.

Known scale indicators include:
- **Revenue:** approximately **$313.3M**
- **Employees:** about **1,000+**; Apollo estimates roughly **1,400**
- **Locations:** customer-provided figure **70**; official/investor sources indicate **70+ to 80+**
- **Geography:** U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico referenced in company/investor materials

## Market Position
Aramsco positions itself as a **leading specialty distributor** in its categories. Its website describes the business as the **largest provider of solutions** to restoration, cleaning, concrete surface preparation, stone fabrication, janitorial and sanitation, asbestos and lead abatement, and environmental cleanup professionals in the U.S. Third-party sources characterize its end markets as **fragmented and competitive**, with Aramsco differentiated by its branch network, just-in-time delivery, technical support, and specialized product breadth.

## History
- **1966:** Founded as a regional industrial safety supplier
- **2005:** Received investment from **Summit Partners**
- **2013:** Acquired by **AEA Investors**; at the time Aramsco had **19 branches** and **200+ employees**

## Overview
**A. Raymond (ARaymond)** is a **family-owned French manufacturer** specializing in **fastening, assembly, and fluid-handling solutions**. The company was **founded in 1865** in **Grenoble, France** by **Albert-Pierre Raymond** and remains under **Raymond family ownership**. Its headquarters are still in **Grenoble, in the French Alps**.

ARaymond serves a range of industrial sectors, with roots in automotive and expansion into **energy, healthcare, construction, agriculture, and broader industrial markets**. The company positions itself as a global engineering and manufacturing partner focused on making customer assembly processes **faster, safer, and more sustainable**.

## Products & Services
ARaymond designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of assembly components and systems, including:
- **Fastening systems** such as clips, press studs, spring clips, panel fasteners, cable and tube holders, and push-on retainers
- **Fluid-handling solutions** including **quick connectors**, cleaning systems, high-tech tubes, pneumatics, and temperature-sensor-related components
- **Industrial assembly solutions** for HVAC, appliances, lighting, plumbing fixtures, furniture, industrial machinery, and electrical equipment
- **Thermal management and EV-related solutions**, including **high-voltage routing** and solutions for electric mobility
- **Bonding and value-added assembly solutions** for specialized industrial applications

Its offerings are designed to reduce assembly time, simplify installation, and lower customers’ **total cost of ownership (TCO)**.

## Scale
ARaymond operates as a global network with significant manufacturing reach:
- **Founded:** 1865
- **Headquarters:** Grenoble, France
- **Geographic footprint:** **25 countries**
- **Employees:** **8,000-8,500+** globally
- **Manufacturing plants:** official sources indicate roughly **27-29 plants**
- **Revenue:** approximately **$1.8 billion** (user-provided / third-party estimate); ARaymond also references **billion-euro annual revenue** on its corporate site

The company describes itself as financially strong and globally distributed, with local operating companies supporting customers across regions.

## Market Position
ARaymond is widely described as a **global expert** and **one of the leaders in fastening and assembly solutions**, especially in automotive and adjacent industrial markets. Historically strong in **mobility/automotive**, it has expanded into growth areas such as **solar energy, healthcare, and electrification-related thermal management**.

Its long-standing differentiation appears to rest on:
- **160+ years of fastening expertise**
- Deep engineering and co-development capabilities
- Global manufacturing presence with local customer support
- Continued investment in new markets tied to **EVs, sustainability, and industrial efficiency**

## History
ARaymond began in **1865** as a workshop producing fastening solutions for gloves and footwear. Its best-known early innovation was the **press stud (snap fastener)**, patented by founder **Albert-Pierre Raymond** in **1886**, which became a worldwide commercial success.

Key milestones in the company’s development include:
- **1925:** launch of the **Vitex zipper**
- **1935:** development of the first **spring steel clip** for the automotive industry
- **1955:** start of **plastic molding** processes
- **1989:** launch of first-generation **quick connectors** for automotive fuel systems
- **2009:** acquisition of **Tinnerman Palnut**
- **2021:** acquisitions including **Castello Italia** and **CGA Technologies** to strengthen thermal-management and fluid-system capabilities

Over six generations, ARaymond has evolved from a fastening inventor into a diversified global manufacturer serving multiple industrial end markets.

## Overview
**Arcosa, Inc.** is a public U.S. manufacturer of **infrastructure-related products and solutions** serving the **construction, engineered structures, and transportation** markets. The company was **spun off from Trinity Industries on November 1, 2018** and trades on the **NYSE under the ticker ACA**. Arcosa is headquartered at **500 N. Akard St., Suite 400, Dallas, Texas 75201**.

Arcosa describes itself as a provider with leading positions across essential infrastructure categories, supported by a portfolio of established operating businesses with long industry histories. The company emphasizes growth through a mix of **organic expansion and disciplined acquisitions**.

## Products & Services
Arcosa operates through **three principal business segments**:

- **Construction Products**
  - Natural and recycled aggregates
  - Specialty materials including lightweight aggregates, gypsum, limestone minerals, and related building products
  - Construction site support equipment such as trench shoring and shielding systems
- **Engineered Structures**
  - Utility structures for transmission, distribution, and substations
  - Concrete and steel pole products for lighting, traffic, electric distribution, and telecom
  - Telecom and traffic structures
  - Structural wind towers
- **Transportation Products**
  - Inland barges
  - Marine hardware and winches under brands such as **NABRICO** and **Wintech**
  - Other transportation and industrial components

## Scale
- **Revenue:** **$2.6 billion** in **2024**
- **Employees:** about **6,250-6,300**
- **Headquarters phone:** **+1 972-942-6500**
- **Locations:** user-provided footprint of **150 locations**
- Arcosa states it has **85+ years operating** across its legacy businesses
- Operations are concentrated primarily in the **United States**, with some presence in **Mexico**

## Market Position
Arcosa is positioned as a **mid-cap infrastructure manufacturer** with leading or strong positions in selected niches such as **aggregates, utility and traffic structures, wind towers, inland barges, and marine components**. Its strategy has increasingly shifted the portfolio toward **construction materials and engineered structures**, markets tied to long-term drivers such as:

- Replacement of aging transportation infrastructure
- Growth in electric transmission and distribution
- Renewable power generation, especially wind
- Expansion of telecom and municipal infrastructure

By 2024, management said **Construction Products represented nearly two-thirds of adjusted EBITDA**, reflecting a deliberate move toward higher-margin, less cyclical businesses.

## History
- **2017-2018:** Trinity Industries announced and executed the spin-off of its infrastructure-related businesses into Arcosa.

- **2024:** Acquired **Ameron Pole Products** for about **$180 million**, expanding its engineered structures offering.
- **October 2024:** Completed the **$1.2 billion acquisition of Stavola's construction materials business**, adding a scaled aggregates and asphalt platform in the New York-New Jersey market.
- **2024:** Also divested its steel components business as part of portfolio simplification.

Overall, Arcosa has evolved from a Trinity spin-off into a more focused infrastructure products company with growing exposure to **aggregates and engineered structures**.

## Overview
**Arjo** is a Swedish **medical device manufacturer** focused on products and solutions that support mobility, patient handling, hygiene, pressure injury prevention, disinfection, diagnostics, and venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention in healthcare settings. The company was **founded in 1957** by **Arne Johansson** in **Eslöv, Sweden**. Its head office and central R&D function are in **Malmö, Sweden**. Arjo is a **public company** listed on **Nasdaq Stockholm** under **ARJO-B**.

Arjo serves hospitals, long-term care providers, and other public and private healthcare institutions, with a stated focus on improving outcomes and quality of life for people with reduced mobility and age-related health challenges.

## Products & Services
Arjo’s portfolio includes:
- **Patient handling** equipment such as ceiling lifts, floor lifters, standing and raising aids, and slings
- **Medical beds** and therapeutic surfaces
- **Personal hygiene** and bathing systems
- **Disinfection** solutions
- **Pressure injury prevention** products, including mattress systems
- **VTE prevention** and **diagnostic** solutions
- Related **services** such as product training, clinical consulting, rental/financing, and healthcare facility design support

Notable legacy products cited in company history include the **first height-adjustable bathtub** launched in **1972**, the **SARA** standing and raising aid introduced in **1989**, and the **Maxi Move** patient lifter system.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approx. **SEK 11 billion in 2023** (roughly aligned with the provided **$1.036B** revenue figure)
- **Employees:** approximately **6,500 worldwide**
- **Geographic reach:** products and services sold in **more than 100 countries**
- **Operations:** **five product development and production units worldwide**
- Third-party sources also indicate a broad international footprint, including around **70 locations** globally

## Market Position
Arjo describes itself as a **market-leading supplier** in its categories, and external sources characterize it as a **global medical device supplier** with strong positions in patient mobility, hygiene, medical beds, and pressure injury prevention. The company operates in both **acute care** and **long-term care** markets, with revenue exposure across **Western Europe, North America, and the rest of the world**. Reported competitors in certain product segments include **Hill-Rom, Guldmann, Handicare, Etac,** and **Invacare**.

## History
Arjo began as a manufacturer of components and machine parts, then expanded into specialized healthcare equipment as Arne Johansson identified demand for bathing and transfer equipment and better ergonomics for caregivers. By the **late 1960s**, the company had expanded into **Western Europe** and established sales companies in markets including the **UK, Germany, France, Belgium, and the US**.

In the **1980s**, Arjo strengthened its international position through acquisitions such as **Century** (US) and **Mecanaids** (UK). The company was first listed in **1993** on the Stockholm and London stock exchanges, then was **acquired by Getinge in 1995**, becoming the foundation of Getinge’s Extended Care business area. Arjo later returned to public markets when it was **spun off from Getinge and listed independently on Nasdaq Stockholm in December 2017**.

## Overview
**Array Technologies, Inc.** is a U.S.-founded manufacturer of solar tracking technology for **utility-scale solar** projects. Founded in **1989** and headquartered at **3901 Midway Place NE, Albuquerque, New Mexico**, the company designs and manufactures systems that orient solar panels to improve energy yield. Array is publicly traded on **NASDAQ: ARRY** and positions itself as a global provider of renewable energy solutions.

The company’s core focus is on durable, large-scale tracker systems engineered for harsh weather conditions, supported by software, field services, and project lifecycle support. Array expanded its international footprint significantly through the **2022 acquisition of STI Norland**, a European tracker manufacturer.

## Products & Services
Array’s offerings center on **solar tracker hardware and related software/services** for utility-scale and distributed solar projects. Key products and solutions include:

- **DuraTrack®** single-axis solar tracker
- **STI H250™** dual-row tracker system
- **OmniTrack™** tracker for challenging terrain
- **SkyLink** photovoltaic-powered control tracker system
- **SmarTrack®** software and controls for performance optimization
- **Fixed-tilt systems**, **foundation solutions**, and **field services**
- Training, commissioning, and support services for solar project deployment

Its customers include solar developers, EPC firms, independent power producers, utilities, and asset owners.

## Scale
- **Headquarters:** Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA
- **Founded:** 1989
- **Employees:** about **1,021-1,100** (2024-2025 sources)
- **Locations:** Company materials indicate global operations across **North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific**; source data provided lists **4 locations**
- **Revenue:** approximately **$915.8 million in 2024** (GlobalData); user-provided figure: **$1,284.1M**
- **2025 performance:** Array reported **40% full-year revenue growth** and a **$2.2 billion orderbook** at year-end 2025

## Market Position
Array describes itself as a **leading American company and global provider of utility-scale solar tracker technology**. Following the STI Norland acquisition, the company stated it became the **largest solar tracker company in the world** by combined scale and manufacturing footprint. Its market position is strongest in utility-scale solar tracking, where reliability, wind resilience, and lifecycle support are central differentiators.

Major competitors commonly cited in the tracker market include **Nextracker** and other solar mounting/tracker manufacturers.

## History
- **1989:** Founded in Albuquerque, New Mexico; Apollo data attributes founding to **Ron Corio**.
- **1990s-2000s:** Built its reputation around rugged tracker designs for utility-scale solar installations.
- **2020:** Completed its public listing on NASDAQ under ticker **ARRY**.
- **January 2022:** Acquired **STI Norland**, expanding manufacturing, engineering, and market access across Europe and Brazil.
- **2025-2026:** Continued expanding beyond trackers into fixed-tilt products, software systems, foundation solutions, and services while maintaining a strong global project pipeline.

Overall, Array Technologies is an established solar equipment manufacturer with more than three decades in the market and a strong position in utility-scale solar tracking.

## Overview
**Arxada** is a global **specialty chemicals manufacturer** headquartered in **Basel, Switzerland**. The company was **founded in 2021** through the carve-out of **Lonza Specialty Ingredients**, acquired by **Bain Capital and Cinven**, and strengthened by the merger with **Troy Corporation** and the acquisition of **Enviro Tech**. Arxada focuses on chemistry- and biotechnology-based solutions that help customers protect products, infrastructure, health, and nutrition.

The company describes itself as a leader in **microbial control solutions** and **performance additives**, serving customers in **more than 100 countries**.

## Products & Services
Arxada offers a broad portfolio across multiple end markets, with core capabilities in:

- **Microbial control solutions**
- **Biocidal active ingredients**
- **Preservatives and disinfectants**
- **Performance additives and specialty chemicals**
- **Wood protection chemicals**
- **Paints and coatings additives**
- **Home & personal care ingredients**
- **Professional hygiene solutions**
- **Human health & nutrition solutions**
- **Food, beverage, and water treatment products**
- **CDMO services** for process development, scale-up, technology transfer, and commercial production

Example product brands featured by the company include **Geogard®**, **PeraGuard®**, **Tanalith® E**, **Tanasote®**, and **NUGEN®**.

## Scale
Arxada reported **CHF 2.0 billion in sales in 2024**. Public company materials and Apollo data indicate the business has approximately **3,200 employees**.

Key operating footprint details include:
- **24 manufacturing sites**
- **14 R&D centers**
- Customers in **100+ countries**
- Around **7,200 customers** (per company presentation)
- Approximately **500 active granted patents**

Its footprint spans Europe, North America, Latin America, Asia-Pacific, Africa, and Oceania.

## Market Position
Arxada positions itself as a **global leader in specialty chemicals**, particularly in **microbial control** and **preservation technologies**. Company materials state it offers one of the market’s **largest selections of biocidal active ingredients** and a broad range of preservative and disinfectant options. Its competitive positioning is supported by:

- Deep **regulatory and formulation expertise**
- Global manufacturing and R&D infrastructure
- Strong presence in essential, regulated end markets
- Backward integration at **Visp, Switzerland**
- Established IP portfolio and long legacy businesses

## History
Arxada’s roots extend well before its 2021 formation through legacy businesses including **Lonza (founded 1897)**, **Troy Corporation (1950)**, and **Enviro Tech (1991)**.

Major milestones:
- **2021:** Arxada formed from the carve-out of Lonza Specialty Ingredients
- **December 2021:** Merger with **Troy Corporation**
- **December 2021:** Acquisition of **Enviro Tech**
- **2024:** Reported **CHF 2 billion** in sales

Today, Arxada operates as a private, global specialty chemicals company centered on preservation, microbial control, and sustainability-driven performance chemistry.

## Overview
**Asahi Intecc Co., Ltd.** is a Japan-based **R&D-oriented medical device manufacturer** that develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices, while also producing **ultra-fine stainless steel wire ropes** and related processed components. The company was **established on July 8, 1976** and is headquartered at **3-100 Akatsuki-cho, Seto, Aichi 489-0071, Japan**. Its President & CEO is **Kenji Miyata**. Asahi Intecc is publicly listed on the **Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market** and **Nagoya Stock Exchange Premier Market** under securities code **7747**.

## Products & Services
- **Medical devices** for catheter-based interventions, especially:
  - **PCI guide wires**
  - **Guiding catheters**
  - **Balloon catheters**
  - **Penetration catheters**
  - **Microcatheters**
- Products used in multiple therapeutic areas:
  - **Cardiovascular/coronary**
  - **Peripheral vascular**
  - **Abdominal vascular**
  - **Cerebrovascular/neurovascular**
- **OEM/ODM services** for medical device partners
- **Medical components** and **industrial components**
- **Ultra-fine stainless steel wire ropes** and **terminal-processed products**

The company emphasizes an **integrated in-house production model**, spanning raw material processing through final product manufacturing.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** **$830.6M** (2025, from provided/reputable profile sources)
- **Employees:** **9,473 consolidated** and **1,196 standalone** as of **June 30, 2025**
- **Capital:** **¥18,860 million** (as of end of June 2025)
- **Locations:** user-provided count of **27 locations**
- Headquarters phone: **+81-561-48-5551**

Asahi Intecc operates globally through subsidiaries and sales bases in countries including **Japan, Thailand, China, the U.S., the Netherlands, Germany, Vietnam, Brazil, the Philippines, and Russia**.

## Market Position
Asahi Intecc is regarded as a **leading maker of high-tech medical devices** in catheter intervention and highlights that it holds a **large share of the global market** for certain device categories on its corporate site. The **Medical Business** is its core earnings driver, complemented by a **Device Business** supplying components for medical and industrial applications. Its positioning is strengthened by long-standing expertise in **fine wire processing**, a core enabling technology for guidewires and catheter devices.

## History
- **1976:** Founded as **Asahi Mini Rope Co., Ltd.**; began selling ultra-fine stainless steel ropes.
- **1988:** Changed company name to **Asahi Intecc Co., Ltd.**
- **1989:** Established **Asahi Intecc Thailand** as an overseas production base.
- **1991:** Opened its **Medical Development Headquarters** and began medical device R&D; started operation of the **Seto Medical Factory**.

- **2020-2024:** Expanded international sales and healthcare footprint, including new entities in **Europe, Germany, the CIS region, the U.S.**, and a specialized heart center initiative in **Kenya**.

## Overview
**Ascend Performance Materials** is a privately held chemical manufacturer focused on **high-performance materials**, especially **nylon 6,6 / PA66**, engineered plastics, fibers, and chemical intermediates. The company is **headquartered in Houston, Texas** (1010 Travis St., Suite 900) and identifies itself as a **fully integrated material solutions provider** with manufacturing operations in **North America, Europe, and Asia**. Its products are used in applications such as **automotive, e-mobility, electrical/electronics, healthcare, textiles, consumer goods, and industrial products**.

Ascend was formed in **2009** when **SK Capital Partners** acquired Solutia’s nylon business and renamed it Ascend Performance Materials. The business, however, traces its industrial roots back to **1953**, when Chemstrand established the first fully integrated U.S. nylon plant in Pensacola, Florida.

## Products & Services
Ascend’s portfolio centers on **nylon and specialty materials** across the value chain, from chemicals to finished compounds and fibers. Key offerings include:
- **PA66 and PA6 resins and compounds** under brands such as **Vydyne®**
- **Flame-retardant resins and compounds** under **Starflam®**
- **Specialty polyamides** under **HiDura™**
- **Circular/recycled polyamides** under **ReDefyne™**
- **Specialty chemicals**, including battery additive **Trinohex® Ultra**
- **Fibers, textile materials, and industrial fiber products**

The company emphasizes its position as the **world’s largest fully integrated producer of nylon 6,6 resin** and highlights use cases in safer vehicles, cleaner energy, medical devices, appliances, apparel, carpets, airbags, cable ties, and circuit boards.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$2.7 billion** (user-provided)
- **Employees:** sources vary from about **2,100-2,500 employees** to **over 3,500 employees and contractors**
- **Locations:** **9 global locations** (company materials and LinkedIn)
- **Regional offices:** **Houston, Shanghai, Brussels, and Detroit**
- **Manufacturing footprint:** facilities across the **U.S., Europe, and Asia**, including major integrated sites in the southeastern United States

## Market Position
Ascend operates in the **chemical manufacturing / performance materials** market and is recognized for its integrated nylon 6,6 capabilities. Its market positioning is strongest in **PA66 resins, engineered thermoplastics, fibers, and intermediates**. The company competes broadly with large chemical and materials producers serving transportation, electronics, industrial, and medical markets.

Ascend’s differentiation comes from its **vertically integrated production base**, scale in **nylon 6,6**, and growing portfolio in **specialty and circular materials**.

## History
- **1953:** Chemstrand establishes a fully integrated nylon plant in Pensacola, Florida
- **1961:** Monsanto acquires Chemstrand
- **1997:** Monsanto spins off its chemicals business into **Solutia Inc.**
- **2009:** **SK Capital Partners** acquires Solutia’s nylon business for **$50 million** and forms **Ascend Performance Materials**
- **2018-2024:** Ascend expands internationally through acquisitions and compounding assets in Europe, Asia, Mexico, and India
- **2025:** Ascend completed a **Chapter 11 restructuring** and **emerged in December 2025** with **Patrick Schumacher** appointed CEO and ownership transferred to a new lender-backed group

Overall, Ascend is an established global manufacturer built around a legacy nylon franchise, with a current focus on engineered materials, specialty chemicals, and advanced applications.

## Overview
**Astec Industries, Inc.** is a publicly traded U.S. manufacturer of heavy equipment and systems used in **asphalt road building, aggregate processing, mining, and concrete production**. The company was **founded on August 9, 1972** and is headquartered at **1725 Shepherd Road, Chattanooga, Tennessee**. It trades on the **NASDAQ** under the ticker **ASTE**.

Astec describes its offering as **“rock to road”** solutions—covering equipment used from material extraction and crushing through asphalt mixing, paving, and related infrastructure work. The company was founded by **Dr. J. Don Brock** along with **Norm Smith, Al Guth, Gail Mize, and Mike Uchytil**.

## Products & Services
Astec manufactures and services equipment across two primary business segments:

- **Infrastructure Solutions**
  - Asphalt plants and related components
  - Asphalt pavers and material transfer vehicles
  - Concrete batch plants and concrete material handling systems
  - Thermal and storage solutions, burners, heaters, tanks, and control systems
  - Telematics, plant controls, retrofits, engineering, and environmental permitting services
- **Materials Solutions**
  - Crushing, screening, and washing equipment
  - Mobile and modular plants
  - Bulk material handling and conveying systems
  - Plant automation and mineral processing equipment
  - Consulting, parts, and aftermarket support

The company states it offers **more than 100 products** and supports customers with training, service, parts, and technical support.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$1.3 billion in 2024**
- **Employees:** about **4,148-4,300 worldwide**
- **Locations:** CRM indicates **16 locations**
- **Geographic footprint:** operations in **12 countries**
- **Brands:** Astec reports **16 trusted brands**

Astec’s sales and manufacturing footprint spans the **U.S., Canada, Brazil, South Africa, and the U.K.**, with additional marketing and service presence in countries including **Australia, Chile, and Thailand**.

## Market Position
Astec is positioned as a **leading global manufacturer** in roadbuilding and materials processing equipment. It has strong brand recognition in **infrastructure, aggregates, and mining equipment**, and historical sources identify it as the **world’s largest manufacturer of asphalt plants**. Its aftermarket business is strategically important, with investor materials noting recurring parts revenue at roughly **30% of total revenue**.

## History
Astec began in **1972** after Dr. Brock left CMI’s asphalt division when that business was being relocated. The founders borrowed **$400,000** to acquire a **24,000-square-foot** building in Chattanooga. The company generated about **$5 million in sales in its first year**.

Briggs & Stratton’s portfolio spans both components and finished equipment, sold under a multi-brand strategy that includes **Briggs & Stratton**, **Vanguard**, **Ferris**, **Simplicity**, **Snapper**, **Billy Goat**, and **Branco**.

Key product categories include:
- **Small gasoline engines** for push mowers, riding mowers, utility equipment, and snow blowers
- **Portable generators** and **home standby generators**
- **Battery storage / energy storage systems** and **lithium-ion battery solutions**
- **Pressure washers**
- **Lawn and garden equipment**
- **Turf care and job-site products**
- **Replacement parts, manuals, dealer support, and service network support**

## Scale
Briggs & Stratton is a large industrial manufacturer with reported revenue around **$1.4 billion** and approximately **3,700-3,800 employees**. Apollo lists **3,700 employees**, while PitchBook cites **3,800**.

- **HQ phone:** +1 414-259-5333
- **13 locations** provided in input; external sources also indicate a broad manufacturing and office footprint
- Products marketed and serviced in **100+ countries**
- Manufacturing and operations footprint across U.S. sites including **Wauwatosa, WI; Poplar Bluff, MO; Auburn, AL; Statesboro, GA; Sherrill/Munnsville, NY** and additional international offices/facilities

Briggs & Stratton holds a longstanding leadership position in outdoor power equipment. ## History
Briggs & Stratton began as a partnership focused on the early automobile market, initially producing **automotive parts** such as locks, switches, igniters, and starter components. In **1919**, it acquired the **A.O. Smith Motor Wheel**, which helped steer the company toward small-engine development. The launch of the **Type P engine in 1920** became an important milestone in establishing its engine business.

Over the following decades, the company expanded through product innovation and acquisitions, including **Simplicity Manufacturing (2004)** and **Billy Goat Industries (2015)**. In **1953**, Briggs & Stratton introduced a lightweight aluminum engine that became influential in the lawn and garden market. In **2020**, the company filed for Chapter 11 and was subsequently acquired by **KPS Capital Partners**, continuing operations as a privately held manufacturer.

## Overview
**Busch Vacuum Solutions** is a **family-owned German manufacturer** of vacuum pumps, vacuum systems, blowers, compressors, and related vacuum/overpressure solutions. The company was **founded in 1963** by **Dr. Karl Busch and Ayhan Busch** and is headquartered in **Maulburg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany**. Busch positions itself as a leading global supplier of industrial vacuum technology and, together with **Pfeiffer Vacuum+Fab Solutions**, operates under the broader **Busch Group**.

Busch offers a broad portfolio of industrial equipment and services, including:
- **Vacuum pumps**
- **Compressors**
- **Blowers**
- **Vacuum systems** (standardized and custom-engineered)
- **Measurement equipment**
- **Leak detectors**
- **Software and connected/monitoring solutions**
- **Spare parts, maintenance, repair, and remanufacturing services**

Its technologies include oil-lubricated rotary vane, dry screw, claw, liquid ring, and other vacuum solutions used across industries such as **food packaging, chemicals, plastics, semiconductors, medical technology, analytics/laboratories, and woodworking**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$2.2 billion** (company-provided revenue figure aligns with third-party estimates)
- **Employees:** official sources indicate roughly **8,000 employees worldwide** at the Busch Group level; some Busch Vacuum Solutions-only sources cite lower figures
- **Global footprint:** about **110 subsidiaries** in roughly **45-47 countries**
- **Production sites:** around **20 production sites** globally at the group level; Busch materials also reference manufacturing across countries including **China, Czech Republic, France, Germany, India, Romania, South Korea, Switzerland, the UK, the USA, and Vietnam**

## Market Position
Busch describes itself as a **world leader in vacuum solutions** and has been recognized by German business media as a **World Market Leader** in vacuum pumps and systems for the **food industry**. The company states that it has been the **world market leader in vacuum packaging for decades**. Its **R5 rotary vane vacuum pump** became an industry standard, with official company materials citing **more than 3 million pumps in operation worldwide**.

## History
- **1963:** Founded as **Dr.-Ing. Karl Busch GmbH** by Ayhan and Dr. Karl Busch in Germany
- **1963:** Developed the **HUCKEPACK**, the first oil-lubricated rotary vane vacuum pump designed specifically for food packaging
- **1969:** Introduced the **R5**, which became the standard in vacuum packaging
- **1971:** Opened its first overseas subsidiary in the **United Kingdom**
- **1972:** Relocated headquarters to **Maulburg**
- **1979:** Established its first production plant outside Germany in the **United States**
- **1981:** Became the **first German industrial company to start manufacturing in China** after reopening
- **1993:** Introduced **COBRA dry screw vacuum pumps**
- **1995:** Launched **MINK claw vacuum pumps**
- **2020s:** Expanded digital/connected vacuum offerings and continued global growth under the Busch Group structure, including the addition of **Pfeiffer Vacuum AG** to the group

Overall, Busch Vacuum Solutions is a long-established industrial manufacturer with a large global installed base, strong presence in vacuum packaging, and a broad portfolio serving multiple process industries.

- A large dedicated service and installation workforce
- National account capabilities for multi-site customers
- Strong emphasis on **safety**, standardized training, and customer service
- Longstanding specialization in commercial roof maintenance, repair, and replacement

Key milestones include:

## Overview
**Cervus Equipment** was a Canadian equipment dealership and distribution company serving the **agriculture, transportation, and industrial/material-handling** markets. The company was founded in **1982**, when **Peter Lacey** and **John Donald** acquired their first John Deere farm equipment dealership. Its corporate headquarters were in **Calgary, Alberta, Canada**.

Before being acquired, Cervus described itself as a leading equipment solutions provider across **Canada, Australia, and New Zealand**. It was publicly traded on the **Toronto Stock Exchange** under the symbol **CERV** until its acquisition by **Brandt Tractor / The Brandt Group of Companies** in **October 2021**.

## Products & Services
Cervus operated authorized dealerships for major OEM brands and generated revenue through equipment sales plus aftermarket support. Its key offerings included:

- **Agriculture equipment:** primarily **John Deere** machinery
- **Transportation equipment:** **Peterbilt** truck dealerships and related parts/service
- **Industrial/material handling equipment:** brands including **Clark, Sellick, Doosan, JLG, and Baumann**
- **Used equipment** sales
- **Parts and service** support
- **Maintenance and repair**
- **Mobile service vehicles** and field support
- **Rentals** and other dealership support services

## Scale
As of **2020**, Cervus operated **64 dealerships** across its markets:

- **38 agriculture** dealerships
- **18 transportation** dealerships
- **8 industrial** dealerships

Geographically, the network spanned **Alberta, Saskatchewan, British Columbia, Manitoba, Ontario, Australia, and New Zealand**. The company reported a workforce of **more than 1,500 employees** in 2020, with roughly **one-third** of staff made up of technicians. It also operated **over 500 service bays** and a fleet of mobile service vehicles.

The user-provided revenue figure is **$1.228B**; third-party sources vary, so revenue should be treated as approximate unless confirmed from audited filings.

## Market Position
Cervus was regarded as one of the larger dealership networks in its sector and, by 2012, was described as **one of John Deere’s largest dealership networks in North America**. Its multi-segment model diversified exposure across farm machinery, heavy trucks, and material handling equipment. In 2021, Brandt said the acquisition of Cervus created **Canada’s largest-ever equipment dealer network** and helped establish Brandt as the **largest John Deere dealership in the world**.

## History
Key milestones include:

- **1982:** Origins began with the first John Deere dealership acquisition by Peter Lacey and John Donald.
- **2010:** Cervus acquired **60% of Agriturf** in New Zealand.
- **2012:** Increased ownership of Agriturf to **100%**.
- **2010s:** Expanded through acquisitions and diversification into transportation and industrial equipment.
- **2020:** Added Australian John Deere business **J.B. Scott**.
- **August 2021:** Announced agreement to be acquired by Brandt.
- **October 2021:** Acquisition completed after shareholder approval; Cervus transitioned from public to private ownership under Brandt.

Today, Cervus is best understood as the predecessor platform that expanded Brandt’s reach in agriculture, transportation, and material handling.

CLARCOR manufactured a broad portfolio of **original equipment (OEM)** and **aftermarket** filtration products. Its offerings served engines, industrial processes, air quality, and environmental applications.

Notable brands associated with CLARCOR included:
- **Baldwin**
- **Fuel Manager®**
- **PECOFacet**
- **Airguard**
- **Altair**
- **BHA®**
- **Clearcurrent®**
- **Clark Filter**
- **Hastings**
- **United Air Specialists**
- **Purolator**

At the time of its acquisition announcement in **2016**, CLARCOR reported:
- **Annual sales of approximately $1.4 billion**
- **About 6,000 employees worldwide**
- Approximately **30 manufacturing and distribution sites** in the United States
- Public listing on the **NYSE** under ticker **CLC** before the acquisition

The business had a strong recurring revenue profile, with approximately **80% of sales coming from the aftermarket**.

## Market Position
CLARCOR was regarded as a **diversified filtration manufacturer** with a strong position in North America and a broad installed base supporting replacement-filter demand. Its combination of proprietary media, industrial air and liquid filtration technologies, and aftermarket exposure made it strategically attractive to Parker Hannifin.

- **2017**: Acquisition completed; CLARCOR ceased to operate as an independent public company

## Overview
**Cochlear Limited** is an Australian medical device manufacturer focused on **implantable hearing solutions** for people with moderate to profound hearing loss. The company was **founded in 1981** to commercialize the multi-channel cochlear implant technology pioneered by **Professor Graeme Clark**. Its global headquarters are on the **Macquarie University campus in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia** (North Ryde/Macquarie Park area).

Cochlear describes itself as the **global leader in implantable hearing solutions**. It sells products in **more than 180 countries** and has employees in **over 50 countries**.

## Products & Services
Cochlear’s portfolio spans three main areas:
- **Cochlear implants**: primarily the **Cochlear™ Nucleus®** platform, including newer systems such as **Nucleus Nexa™**.
- **Acoustic / bone conduction solutions**: **Cochlear™ Osia®** and **Cochlear™ Baha®** systems.
- **Services and recipient support**: sound processor upgrades, accessories, support apps, and connected-care tools such as **Remote Check**, **Remote Assist**, **Custom Sound® Pro**, **SmartNav**, and **Cochlear Link**.

The company’s model includes both initial implant sales and a recurring base of **processor upgrades, accessories, and long-term recipient support**.

## Scale
- **FY2025 sales revenue:** **$2,355.8 million**
- **FY2024 sales revenue:** **$2,258.2 million**
- **Employees:** **over 5,500** globally in FY2025 (Apollo estimate: ~5,000)
- **Countries served:** **180+**
- **Employees located in:** **50+ countries**
- **Manufacturing footprint:** facilities in **Australia, Sweden, China, and Malaysia**
- **People helped hear:** **750,000+** by FY2025; company web pages cite **700,000+** recipients earlier
- **Annual R&D investment:** **$290+ million** in FY2025

## Market Position
Cochlear has held a leading position in hearing implants for decades. Its annual reports state it maintained **global market share above 60%** in FY2025 and reported **over 60%** share in FY2024. The company positions this leadership around product reliability, long-term clinical evidence, and sustained R&D investment.

Its business is diversified across **cochlear implants, acoustics, and services**, with cochlear implants remaining the largest segment. In FY2025, cochlear implants represented about **62%** of revenue, services **26%**, and acoustics **12%**.

## History

- **1967:** Professor Graeme Clark begins research into restoring hearing.
- **1978:** First successful implantation of a **multi-channel cochlear implant**.
- **1981:** Cochlear is established in Australia.

- **2025:** Launch of the **Cochlear™ Nucleus® Nexa™ System**, described by the company as the first smart cochlear implant system with upgradeable firmware.

Overall, Cochlear is a long-established, large-scale hearing implant specialist with a leading global position in its category.

## Overview

(NASDAQ: DSGR)** is a specialty industrial distributor providing **high-touch, value-added distribution solutions** to the **maintenance, repair and operations (MRO)**, **original equipment manufacturer (OEM)**, and **industrial technologies** markets. ## Overview
**Diversey** is a global manufacturer of **cleaning, hygiene, infection prevention, and sanitation solutions** for commercial and institutional customers. Founded in **1923** in **Chicago** by **August and Herbert Kochs**, the business is now headquartered in **Fort Mill, South Carolina**. Diversey serves sectors including **hospitality, healthcare, food and beverage, food service, retail, and facility management**. Its solutions are positioned around operational hygiene, food safety, infection prevention, and sustainability.

## Products & Services
Diversey offers an integrated portfolio that combines:
- **Cleaning and disinfecting chemicals**
- **Dosing and dispensing systems**
- **Floor care machines and tools**
- **Laundry, housekeeping, room care, and hand hygiene solutions**
- **Food safety and sanitation programs**
- **Water and energy management solutions**

- **Geographic reach:** operations in **over 80 countries**

Public deal materials described the company as serving more than **85,000 customers** globally.

## Overview
**DNOW Inc.** is a publicly traded industrial distributor focused on the energy and broader industrial markets, best known as a leading distributor of **pipe, valves and fittings (PVF)**, along with pumps, gas products, fabricated equipment and MRO supplies. The company is headquartered at **7402 N. Eldridge Parkway, Houston, Texas 77041**, and trades on the **NYSE under the ticker DNOW**. DNOW was incorporated in **2013** and became an independent public company on **June 2, 2014** through the spin-off of National Oilwell Varco's distribution business. The company officially changed its corporate name from **NOW Inc. to DNOW Inc. in January 2024**.

## Products & Services
DNOW distributes a broad portfolio of products used to build, maintain and operate energy and industrial infrastructure, including:
- **PVF products:** pipe, valves, fittings, flanges, gaskets and fasteners
- **Pumps and process equipment**
- **Electrical, instrumentation and measurement products**
- **Artificial lift, drilling and production equipment**
- **Industrial supplies, safety products, PPE and MRO consumables**
- **Packaged and engineered process/production equipment**

Its service offering extends beyond product distribution to include:
- **Supply chain and materials management**
- **Procurement, logistics, inventory and warehouse management**
- **Valve actuation, inspection, testing and repair**
- **Technical support, field services and equipment rental**
- **Digital commerce and data tools through DigitalNOW®**

## Scale
DNOW reported **full-year 2024 revenue of $2.373 billion** and **full-year 2025 revenue of $2.8 billion** following completion of its MRC Global combination in late 2025. Company sources cited approximately **2,575 employees** before the merger; after completing the MRC Global transaction on **November 6, 2025**, DNOW reported approximately **5,300 employees** and a global network of distribution and engineering locations. The company states it has a strong worldwide footprint centered in North America, with operations serving customers across multiple international regions.

## Market Position
DNOW positions itself as a **premier energy and industrial solutions provider** and a major PVF distributor serving **upstream, midstream, downstream, gas utilities, industrial, mining, municipal water, engineering and construction, and energy transition** markets. Its differentiation comes from combining large-scale distribution with technical product expertise, engineered equipment capabilities, value-added services and digital procurement tools. The **2025 acquisition of MRC Global** significantly expanded DNOW's scale and strengthened its position in the PVF and energy/industrial infrastructure distribution market.

## History
DNOW traces its heritage back more than **160 years**, with legacy roots in companies such as **Oilwell Supply (1878)**, **National Supply (1894)** and **Wilson Supply (1921)**. Those businesses became part of the National Oilwell / NOV lineage over time. Key milestones include:
- **2014:** Distribution business spun off from NOV to form **NOW Inc. / DistributionNOW**
- **2024:** Corporate name changed to **DNOW Inc.**
- **2024:** Acquired **Whitco Supply** and **Trojan Rentals**
- **2025:** Completed all-stock combination with **MRC Global**, creating a larger, more diversified energy and industrial distribution platform

## Overview
**Dresser-Rand** is a U.S.-based engineering and manufacturing company that designs, manufactures, and services **rotating equipment** for the **oil & gas, petrochemical, power, and process industries**. Its core offerings include compressors, turbines, engines, and related systems used in critical energy infrastructure applications.

The business traces its operating roots back to **1986**, when **Dresser Industries** and **Ingersoll-Rand** combined certain operations in a joint venture. The current corporate entity, **Dresser-Rand Group Inc.**, was formed in **2004**. The company is headquartered in **Houston, Texas** (10205 Westheimer Road), and historically also maintained a significant presence in **Paris, France**.

Today, Dresser-Rand operates as part of **Siemens Energy**, following Siemens’ acquisition of the company.

## Products & Services
- **Turbo and reciprocating compressors**
- **Steam turbines**
- **Industrial and aeroderivative gas turbines**
- **Diesel and gas engines**
- **Gas expanders**
- **Control panels and modular power solutions**
- **Aftermarket parts, maintenance, repair, and field service**

Its equipment is used in applications such as **oil and gas production, gas transmission, LNG, refining, petrochemicals, power generation, and industrial processing**. The company has emphasized long-life, custom-engineered systems and lifecycle service support.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** about **$3.0 billion** in fiscal **2013**; about **$2.8 billion** in fiscal **2014**
- **Employees:** about **8,100** (2013) and about **7,900** (2014); some later sources cite **11,000+** employees post-acquisition integration
- **Global footprint:** nearly **100,000 rotating equipment units installed** worldwide
- **Geographic reach:** operations or installed base in **more than 150 countries**
- Historical materials cite **12 manufacturing facilities**, roughly **37 service centers**, and **65 sales offices** globally

## Market Position
Dresser-Rand has been regarded as **one of the leading global suppliers of rotating equipment solutions** for energy and process markets. Its strength has historically been in **custom-engineered turbomachinery** and a large **aftermarket/service base**, both important differentiators in oil and gas infrastructure. Siemens described the company in 2014 as a strong strategic fit that expanded Siemens’ portfolio in **compressors, steam turbines, distributed power, and oil & gas applications**.

## History
- **1986:** Dresser Industries and Ingersoll-Rand form the Dresser-Rand joint venture.
- **2004:** Private equity firm **First Reserve** acquires Dresser-Rand; **Dresser-Rand Group Inc.** is organized in Delaware.
- **2005:** The company goes public on the **NYSE** under ticker **DRC**.
- **2012:** Dresser-Rand acquires **Grupo Guascor S.L.** and **Synchrony, Inc.** to broaden its engine and technology portfolio.
- **2014:** **Siemens** announces a friendly takeover valued at approximately **$7.6 billion**.
- **2015:** Siemens completes the acquisition; Dresser-Rand becomes part of Siemens’ energy business.
- **2018:** The **Dresser-Rand Government Business** is sold to **Curtiss-Wright**.

The company’s industrial heritage extends further back through predecessor businesses dating to the **19th century**, particularly legacy compressor and engine operations associated with Dresser and Clark/Dresser-Rand entities.

## Overview

## Overview

- **1908:** Founded in Houston as **Southern Engine and Pump Company** by Charles A. Levins.

## Overview
**Eagle Materials, Inc. (NYSE: EXP)** is a U.S.-based manufacturer of heavy construction products and light building materials. The company was founded in **1963** as a division of Centex Construction and is headquartered in **Dallas, Texas** at **5960 Berkshire Lane, Suite 900, Dallas, TX 75225**. It was renamed **Eagle Materials** in **2004** after being spun off from Centex.

Eagle serves U.S. residential, commercial, industrial, and public infrastructure markets. Its core products—especially **Portland cement** and **gypsum wallboard**—are used in roads, highways, and building construction and renovation.

## Products & Services
Eagle Materials operates through four main business segments:

- **Cement**: Portland cement, including Portland limestone cement
- **Concrete & Aggregates**: ready-mix concrete, crushed stone, sand, and gravel
- **Gypsum Wallboard**: wallboard products for interior construction
