Össur’s growth has come through a combination of **organic innovation** and **strategic acquisitions**, building a broad portfolio in prosthetics and bracing over more than five decades.

## Overview
**OTC Industrial Technologies** is a privately held U.S. industrial distributor and service provider focused on highly engineered solutions for manufacturing and process industries. The company was **founded in 1963** and is headquartered in **Columbus, Ohio** at **3948 Townsfair Way, Suite 200, Columbus, OH 43219**. OTC is also known as **Ohio Transmission Corporation**.

OTC positions itself as a one-stop industrial solutions partner, combining product distribution with engineering, repair, fabrication, and field service. It serves customers across a wide range of sectors including manufacturing, automotive, food and beverage, oil and gas, utilities, steel, life sciences, and water/wastewater.

## Products & Services
OTC distributes and supports a broad portfolio of industrial equipment and components, with particular strength in **fluid power**, **pump systems**, **compressed air**, **power transmission**, **motion control**, **factory automation**, **motors**, **bearings**, and **finishing/dispensing/filtration**.

Key offerings include:
- **Fluid power and motion control** components and systems
- **Pump and fluid handling** equipment for industrial and municipal applications
- **Power transmission** products such as couplings, belts, bushings, sprockets, and clutches
- **Compressed air systems** and engineered compressor solutions
- **Automation and engineered system design**
- **Repair, maintenance, and field service** for multiple equipment types and brands
- **Rental solutions**, spare parts support, and preventative maintenance programs

The company operates through a portfolio of specialized brands and subsidiaries spanning industrial automation, rotating equipment, pump solutions, air systems, and finishing technologies.

## Scale
OTC is one of the larger industrial distributors in its category in the U.S. Available sources indicate:
- **Revenue:** approximately **$875M** (user-provided)
- **Employees:** about **2,000 associates** on the company website; third-party sources cite **1,600+**
- **Locations:** company materials cite **60+ branch locations** across **40+ states**; user-provided figure is **70 locations**
- **Service footprint:** nearly **40 service shops** nationwide (per Genstar Capital)
- **Customers served:** **13,000+** (per Genstar Capital)

## Market Position
OTC describes itself as **one of the largest industrial distributors and service providers in the United States**. Its market position is built on a combination of:
- Broad national coverage
- Deep technical and engineering expertise
- Longstanding partnerships with top-tier OEM vendors
- Strong aftermarket repair and maintenance capabilities
- A multi-brand platform serving diverse industrial niches

The company emphasizes value through improving **uptime**, **labor safety**, **energy conservation**, and overall operational efficiency.

## History
OTC was **established in 1963** and has expanded from its Ohio roots into a national industrial distribution platform. Over time, it has grown both organically and through acquisitions, building a family of specialized companies across automation, pumps, compressed air, power transmission, and related industrial technologies. 

The business is currently backed by **Genstar Capital**, reflecting its evolution into a scaled, multi-brand industrial distribution and services platform with nationwide reach.

## Overview
**PABCO Building Products, LLC** is a **private, family-owned manufacturer of building materials** serving the construction industry in the **western United States and Canada**. The company is headquartered in **Rancho Cordova, California** and is part of **Pacific Coast Building Products, Inc.**, a larger building-products group that traces its roots to **Anderson Lumber, founded in Sacramento in 1953** by **Fred and Pat Anderson**. PABCO Building Products itself grew through manufacturing acquisitions beginning in the **1970s**.

PABCO’s stated business focus is manufacturing quality wallboard, paper, and roofing products, with an emphasis on sustainability, safety, and long-term customer relationships.

## Products & Services
PABCO operates through three main divisions:

- **PABCO Gypsum** – gypsum wallboard and panel products for residential and commercial construction, including:
  - **Flame Curb®**
  - **Sound Curb™**
  - **Abuse Curb®**
  - impact-resistant and glass-mat sheathing products
  - **QuietRock®** sound-reducing drywall
- **PABCO Paper** – industrial paper products made with **100% recycled pre- and post-consumer fiber**, including:
  - gypsum facing and backing paper
  - specialty and packaging papers
  - chip and liner products
- **PABCO Roofing Products** – asphalt roofing materials including:
  - laminated and 3-tab shingles
  - starter, ridge, and cap materials
  - patented **Cascade™** diamond-shaped shingles

## Scale
- **Estimated revenue:** **~$400M** (user-provided)
- **Locations:** **8** (user-provided)
- **Employee count:** third-party estimates vary; Apollo lists **~250 employees**, while Crunchbase lists **501–1,000 employees** for the business
- **Manufacturing capacity:** PABCO Gypsum states its Newark, CA and Las Vegas, NV operations supply **more than 1.65 billion square feet of gypsum board annually**
- **Geographic presence:** products and operations support customers across the **U.S. West and Canada**

## Market Position
PABCO is a **regional building materials manufacturer** with established positions in **gypsum wallboard, recycled paper, and asphalt roofing shingles**. Its market differentiation centers on:

- **vertical integration** across gypsum, paper, and roofing-related materials
- specialty offerings such as **QuietRock®** sound-reducing drywall
- sustainability claims, including recycled paper inputs and environmental programs
- a long-standing reputation as a **family-owned** supplier with strong contractor and distributor relationships

In roofing, PABCO highlights nearly **40 years** of asphalt shingle manufacturing and positions its warranty, service, and patented designs as key competitive strengths.

## History
- **1953:** Parent company origins begin with **Anderson Lumber** in Sacramento
- **1972:** PABCO entered gypsum manufacturing by acquiring an idle wallboard plant in **Newark, California**
- **1977:** Expanded gypsum operations through acquisition of a **Johns-Manville plant and quarry near Las Vegas, Nevada**
- **1984:** Added **PABCO Paper** and acquired roofing operations, establishing **PABCO Roofing Products**
- **1998, 2005, 2009:** Major modernization/expansion investments in Las Vegas and Newark gypsum facilities
- **2013:** Acquired **QuietRock®**, adding a well-known sound-reducing drywall brand
- **2024:** PABCO Roofing Products marked **40 years** in asphalt roofing; parent Pacific Coast Building Products marked **70 years** in 2023

Overall, PABCO has grown through targeted acquisitions and plant modernization into a diversified manufacturer of core building products with a strong West Coast and Western North America footprint.

## Overview
**PALFINGER AG** is an Austrian manufacturer of crane and lifting equipment for land and marine applications. Founded in **1932** by **Richard Palfinger**, the company began as a small workshop for agricultural trailers, tippers, and vehicle bodies and later evolved into a global lifting-technology group. Its headquarters are in **Bergheim, Austria** (Lamprechtshausener Bundesstraße 8). PALFINGER has been **listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange since 1999**.

The company describes itself as a leading technology and mechanical engineering business focused on practical, integrated lifting solutions. Its core franchise is the **hydraulic loader crane**, where it is widely identified as the **world market leader**.

## Products & Services
PALFINGER’s portfolio spans both **LAND** and **MARINE** applications. Main product categories include:

- **Loader cranes** (core product; more than **100 models**)
- **Timber and recycling cranes**
- **Hooklifts and skiploaders**
- **Truck-mounted forklifts**
- **Aerial work platforms / access platforms**
- **Tail lifts and passenger lifts**
- **Railway systems**
- **Marine cranes, winches, offshore equipment, boats and davits**
- **Wind cranes and marine handling solutions**

Beyond equipment, PALFINGER offers lifecycle services such as:
- Global sales and after-sales support
- Spare parts and repair
- Service contracts
- Digital fleet and telematics tools via **PALFINGER Connected / PALDESK**

## Scale
PALFINGER is a large global industrial company with:

- **2024 revenue:** **EUR 2.36 billion**
- **Employees:** about **12,350** worldwide (2024 company figures)
- **Manufacturing sites:** **30** worldwide
- **Reach:** dealer/service presence in **130 countries**
- **Service footprint:** more than **5,000 service points** and over **200 independent general importers**

The company operates internationally with a broad production, assembly, sales, and service footprint across Europe, the Americas, Asia, and other regions.

## Market Position

## Overview
**PAUL HARTMANN AG (HARTMANN GROUP)** is a German manufacturer of medical, hygiene, and care products headquartered in **Heidenheim an der Brenz, Baden-Württemberg, Germany**. Founded in **1818**, the company has over **200 years** of operating history and is publicly traded in Germany under **FRA: PHH2**. HARTMANN focuses on professional healthcare and home-care solutions and sells into hospitals, medical practices, nursing homes, pharmacies, and home-care settings.

The company describes itself as one of the **leading European providers of professional medical and care products and associated services**. It is represented in **36 countries** and sells products in **more than 130 countries** worldwide.

HARTMANN’s core business is organized around four areas:

- **Incontinence Management** – products such as absorbent underwear, pads, pants, fixation products, and skin-care solutions; flagship brand: **MoliCare®**
- **Wound Care & Diagnostics** – wound dressings, post-operative dressings, compression therapy, first aid, immobilization, and home diagnostic devices; brands include **Zetuvit®** and **Cosmopor®**
- **Infection Management** – disinfectants, hygiene products, surgical drapes, operating theater apparel, custom procedure trays, and surgical instruments; flagship brand: **Sterillium®**
- **Complementary Group Divisions** – includes subsidiaries such as **Kneipp**, **CMC**, and **KOB**

Its portfolio spans traditional and advanced wound care, disinfection, surgical consumables, diagnostics, patient care, and selected consumer medical products.

- **Employees:** about **10,079–10,085** in 2024; company materials also state **over 10,000 staff worldwide**
- **Geographic footprint:** **36 countries** with sales in **130+ countries**
- **Primary address:** **Paul-Hartmann-Strasse 12, 89522 Heidenheim, Germany**
- **HQ phone:** **+49 7321 360**

## Market Position
HARTMANN is positioned as a major European medical products supplier with particular strength in **wound care, incontinence, and infection prevention**. The company states it **retained its position as the leading wound care provider in the European pharmacy market in 2024**. Its long-established brands and broad distribution footprint support a strong presence across institutional and home-care channels.

## History
HARTMANN began in **1818**, when **Ludwig von Hartmann** acquired the Meebold spinning mill. The business later evolved under the Hartmann family into a dressing materials company that helped advance modern wound care. The company became a stock corporation in **1912**.

After World War II, international expansion resumed more cautiously; a key milestone was the founding of **HARTMANN-FRANCE S.A. in 1972**, marking renewed foreign investment. In recent years, management has emphasized higher-margin shipping technology, presort services, cost reduction, and cash generation.

## History
- **1920:** Founded as the **Pitney-Bowes Postage Meter Company** after the merger of Arthur Pitney’s and Walter Bowes’ businesses.
- **1920:** Became the first postage meter approved for use across the U.S. postal system.
- **1950:** Listed on the **New York Stock Exchange**.
- **2002:** Acquired **PSI**, becoming the largest presort mail company in the U.S.
- **2007:** Acquired **MapInfo**, expanding into software and location intelligence.
- **2012:** Launched the **Global Shipping Program**, helping marketplace sellers ship internationally.
- **2020:** Marked **100 years** of operations.
- **2024:** Completed a major restructuring and wind-down of most of its **Global Ecommerce** segment, leaving the business centered on **SendTech Solutions** and **Presort Services**.

## Overview
**Pixelle Specialty Solutions** is a U.S.-based manufacturer of specialty papers for **printing, packaging, labeling, and industrial applications**. The company was **formed in 2018** and is headquartered at **228 S. Main Street, Spring Grove, Pennsylvania**. Pixelle describes itself as a leading North American producer of specialty papers, with products made in the U.S. and a legacy of papermaking that traces back to **1864** through its predecessor operations.

## Products & Services
Pixelle offers a broad portfolio of specialty paper grades, including:
- **Barrier papers** and **food papers** for packaging
- **Book papers** and **commercial papers**
- **Carbonless papers** and **forms bond papers**
- **Envelope papers**
- **Label facestock** and other label substrates
- **Casting & release papers**
- **Inkjet media**
- **Opaque papers**
- **Security papers**
- **Heavyweight tag, ledger, and index papers**

Its products serve end markets such as **food packaging, digital and commercial printing, labels, envelopes, greeting cards, security documents, and other converting applications**. The company emphasizes technical capabilities such as **barrier coatings**, customized specialty grades, and collaborative R&D.

## Scale
- **Reported revenue:** **$636.2M**
- **Employee count:** sources vary; Apollo lists about **710** employees, while LinkedIn and other third-party databases place the company in the **1,001-5,000** range and PitchBook reported about **2,105 employees (2022)**.
- **Operations:** Pixelle has operated multiple U.S. paper mills and converting sites. In 2022, the company reported facilities in **Spring Grove, PA; Chillicothe, OH; Jay, ME; Stevens Point, WI; and Fremont, OH**. More recent 2024 company materials refer to operations in **Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin** and mention investment in **three paper mills**.
- **Production scale:** in 2022, Pixelle reported its mills produced **more than 1 million tons of paper annually**.

## Market Position
Pixelle is positioned as a **leading manufacturer of specialty papers in North America**. Company and investor materials describe it as the **leading specialty-focused paper producer in North America**, and external coverage has referred to it as the **largest specialty papers producer in North America** following acquisitions completed in its early years. Its portfolio spans a wide range of technically demanding grades, supporting customers in packaging, labeling, and print markets.

## History
- **1864:** Papermaking legacy begins through the Glatfelter business in Spring Grove, Pennsylvania.
- **2018:** **Pixelle Specialty Solutions** is created after Lindsay Goldberg acquires Glatfelter's specialty papers division.

## Overview
**Ply Gem** is a North American manufacturer of exterior building products for residential construction, repair, remodel, and some commercial applications. The company markets a broad exterior portfolio designed to work together across the home envelope, serving builders, remodelers, contractors, distributors, and homeowners in the U.S. and Canada.

- **Siding and accessories**
- **Windows**
- **Patio doors**
- **Stone veneer**
- **Trim and moulding**
- **Fence and railing**
- **Shutters and exterior accessories**
- **Metal and rainware** such as gutters and related components

## Scale

- **Locations:** **49** (user-provided; also supported by third-party company profiles)

## Overview
**PrimeSource Building Products** is a **private distributor of specialty branded building products** serving residential and commercial new construction and remodeling markets. The company is headquartered in **Irving, Texas** (1321 Greenway Dr.) and was **founded in 1938**. It is owned by **Clearlake Capital Group**, which acquired the business from Platinum Equity in **December 2020**.

PrimeSource positions itself as a **single-source national supplier** for construction-related products, combining proprietary brands with third-party brands and leveraging global sourcing plus a nationwide fulfillment footprint.

PrimeSource distributes a broad portfolio across major construction categories, including:
- **Fastening systems**: nails, screws, collated fasteners, hand-drive fasteners

## Scale

PrimeSource traces its roots to **1938**, though some transaction materials describe the current PrimeSource platform as having been **founded in 1990**, likely reflecting later corporate formation and expansion. Historically known as **Sequoia Supply**, the company evolved into a larger specialty building-products platform through sourcing expansion, brand development, and acquisitions.

## Overview
**Radiometer** is a Danish medical device manufacturer focused on **acute care diagnostics**. The company develops and markets solutions that help clinicians make rapid diagnostic decisions for critically ill patients, especially in hospital and point-of-care settings. Its core areas include **blood gas analysis, immunoassay testing, transcutaneous monitoring, blood sampling, and point-of-care IT/data management**.

Radiometer was **founded in 1935** by **Børge Aagaard Nielsen** and **Carl Schrøder** in **Copenhagen, Denmark**, where it remains headquartered. The company became part of **Danaher’s Diagnostics segment in 2004**.

## Products & Services
Radiometer’s portfolio is centered on acute and critical care workflows. Key offerings include:
- **Blood gas analyzers** for measuring critical parameters such as pH, oxygen, and lactate
- **Immunoassay analyzers** for markers including **cardiac, coagulation, infection, and pregnancy** indicators
- **Transcutaneous monitors** used in neonatal and other monitoring applications
- **Blood sampling products**, including syringes and capillaries
- **Point-of-care IT and data management systems**, including workflow and connectivity solutions such as **AQURE**
- Related **services, support, quality control, and digital/remote insights tools**

The company states that its systems are used to support faster, reliable decisions in emergency, intensive care, neonatal, and other acute care environments.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$857.6M** (provided)
- **Employees:** about **3,900** estimated by Apollo; company materials also cite **more than 3,400 employees worldwide**
- **Locations:** direct representation in **32 countries**; products sold in **more than 120 countries**
- **Headquarters:** **Åkandevej 21, 2700 Brønshøj/Copenhagen, Denmark**
- **HQ phone:** **+45 38 27 38 27**

Danaher notes that **about 500,000 blood samples are tested every day** using Radiometer equipment.

## Market Position
Radiometer is widely positioned as a **leader in acute care diagnostics** and specifically a **pioneer in blood gas testing**. The company emphasizes that it introduced the **world’s first commercially available blood gas analyzer in 1954** and continues to describe itself as a **market leader in blood gas testing**. Its affiliation with **Danaher** strengthens its global reach, distribution, and diagnostic ecosystem presence.

## History
Radiometer began in **1935** as a maker of measuring devices for Denmark’s growing **radio industry**. In **1937**, collaboration with the **Carlsberg Laboratory** led to development work on pH measurement in liquids. During the **polio epidemic of the early 1950s**, clinicians including **Poul Astrup** and **Bjørn Ibsen** used Radiometer’s pH technology to improve blood analysis for patients with respiratory failure.

That work led to a major turning point: in **1954**, Radiometer developed the **first commercially available blood gas analyzer**, marking its entry into medical technology. Since then, the company has expanded into a broader acute care diagnostics portfolio and, after joining **Danaher in 2004**, has continued to grow internationally.

## Overview
**RDO Equipment Co.** is a privately held, family-owned equipment distributor and dealer headquartered in **Fargo, North Dakota**. Founded in **1968** by **Ronald D. Offutt**, the company began with the purchase of a single John Deere dealership in **Casselton, North Dakota**. Today, RDO sells and supports equipment for **agriculture, construction, environmental, irrigation, positioning, and surveying** applications.

The company describes itself as a provider of **intelligently connected equipment** and related support services. Its core manufacturer relationships include **John Deere, Vermeer, Topcon, WIRTGEN GROUP,** and **Carlson**.

## Products & Services
RDO Equipment distributes both **new and used equipment** and also offers **rental options** in certain categories. Product lines span:

- **Agriculture equipment**
- **Construction and forestry equipment**
- **Environmental and recycling equipment**
- **Irrigation systems**
- **Roadbuilding and aggregate equipment**
- **Machine control, positioning, and surveying technology**
- **Lawn and land equipment**

Support services include:

- **Parts and maintenance**
- **Repair and field service**
- **Equipment protection and service plans**
- **Connected support and technology support services**
- **Precision agriculture and machine-control solutions**

## Scale
RDO operates **85 locations across 12 U.S. states** according to its website. Other company materials describe **more than 80 U.S. locations**. The business also cites international partnerships in **Africa, Australia, Mexico, and Ukraine**.

Available headcount estimates cluster around **2,500-2,700 employees**; Apollo estimates **2,500 employees**, while RDO states it has **more than 2,700 team members**, including nearly **375 staff** at its Fargo Field Support Office. Provided revenue is **about $1.7 billion**.

## Market Position
RDO is one of the larger independent equipment dealership groups in the U.S. and has built its market position around major OEM relationships, especially **John Deere**. The company has expanded beyond traditional farm equipment into **construction, roadbuilding, irrigation, and advanced machine technology**, positioning itself as a broad **equipment-and-support solutions provider** rather than only a dealership.

Its participation in purchasing cooperatives such as **BuyBoard, HGAC, NPP, and Sourcewell** also supports public-sector and fleet purchasing access.

## History
RDO’s roots are in farming: founder Ron Offutt was a potato farmer when he acquired the first dealership in **1968**. Expansion accelerated through the **1970s and 1980s** with additional agriculture stores, then into **construction equipment in 1989**.

Major milestones include:

- **1968:** First dealership acquired in Casselton, ND
- **1989:** Entry into construction equipment
- **1997:** Initial public offering and expansion through acquisitions
- **1998-2000:** Diversification into rental, finance, material handling, and trucks
- **2003:** Company taken private again
- **2009:** Establishment of **RDO Integrated Controls** to expand technology offerings
- **2021:** Completion of the Fargo **Field Support Office**

Over time, RDO evolved from a single-store dealership into a multi-state distributor with a strong emphasis on equipment technology, service, and manufacturer partnerships.

## Overview
**Reliable Automatic Sprinkler Co., Inc.** is a privately held **manufacturer and distributor of fire protection products** serving commercial, residential, and specialty fire protection applications. The company was **founded on January 23, 1920** by **Frank J. Fee** and has operated in the fire protection industry for more than a century. 

Reliable’s principal manufacturing operation is in **Liberty, South Carolina** at **1470 Smith Grove Rd**, which is also listed as its corporate manufacturing facility and main phone **+1 864-843-1700**. Some business directories also reference **Elmsford, New York** in connection with the company. Reliable describes itself as a global supplier with regional sales and distribution centers across the U.S. and internationally.

## Products & Services
Reliable manufactures and distributes a broad portfolio of **fire protection equipment**. Its core offerings include:
- **Fire sprinklers** for residential, commercial, and specialty applications
- **Valves** and valve trim
- **System components** such as risers, floor control assemblies, grooved connections, test and drain valves, hose valves, air vents, air compressors, and related accessories
- Products supporting **wet, dry, deluge, preaction, and special hazard systems**

The company positions itself as a **one-stop source** for fire protection products, pairing manufacturing with distribution and customer support.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$334.8M** (user-provided)
- **Employees:** Apollo estimates about **1,300 employees**; LinkedIn lists **1,001–5,000** employees
- **Locations:** **61** locations (user-provided; also reflected by ZoomInfo)
- **Manufacturing footprint:** approximately **467,000+ sq. ft.** at its Liberty, SC facility

Reliable says all of its fire protection valves and sprinklers are manufactured in **Liberty, South Carolina**, where teams for engineering, quality assurance, product development, manufacturing, procurement, marketing, HR, and shipping are based.

## Market Position
Reliable is widely described as a **leader in the fire protection industry** and, in third-party listings, as **one of the world’s largest manufacturers of automatic fire sprinklers and sprinkler system control equipment**. Its market position is built on long tenure, U.S.-based manufacturing, broad product coverage, and an international distribution footprint. The company serves customers globally and emphasizes quality, innovation, and channel partnership rather than competing directly with customers.

## History
- **1920:** Company founded by **Frank J. Fee** as The Reliable Automatic Sprinkler Co. Inc.
- Over the following decades, Reliable expanded from sprinkler manufacturing into a broader fire protection product line.
- **1941:** According to the company’s centennial booklet, Reliable was invited by the **U.S. War Department** to produce automatic sprinkler equipment for hospitals on military bases.
- The company later shifted major manufacturing to **Liberty, South Carolina**, which remains its flagship production site.
- **2020:** Reliable celebrated its **100th anniversary**, highlighting continuity of the founding vision: high-quality U.S.-designed and produced fire protection products backed by service and long-term customer relationships.

## Overview
**Richelieu Hardware Ltd.** is a Canadian **importer, manufacturer, and distributor of specialty hardware and complementary products** for the building materials, woodworking, cabinetry, furniture, and renovation markets. The company was **founded in 1968** and is headquartered in **Montreal, Quebec, Canada** (Saint-Laurent borough).

Richelieu serves professional customers across North America, including **kitchen and bathroom cabinet manufacturers, closet and storage manufacturers, home and office furniture makers, door and window manufacturers, residential and commercial woodworkers, and hardware retailers/renovation superstores**. It is publicly traded on the **Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol RCH**.

## Products & Services
Richelieu operates as a **one-stop-shop distributor** with a very broad catalog of specialty hardware and related products. Its assortment includes:
- **Decorative and functional hardware** for furniture, cabinets, glass, and buildings
- **Hinges, slides, opening systems, screws, and fasteners**
- **Kitchen and bathroom accessories**
- **Closet and storage solutions**
- **Lighting systems and accessories**
- **Sliding door systems**
- **Decorative and functional panels, high-pressure laminates, railings and balusters**
- **Floor protection products and power-tool accessories**

The company also manufactures selected products through subsidiaries and plants in Quebec, including **veneer sheets, edge banding, decorative moldings, and window/door components**. A significant share of its assortment is sold under **private-label and exclusive brands**.

## Scale
As of fiscal **2024**, Richelieu reported approximately **$1.8 billion in sales**. Official company materials cite:
- **112 strategically located centres** across North America as of **November 30, 2024**
- **3 manufacturing plants**
- **More than 120,000 active customers**
- **More than 145,000 SKUs**
- **5.1 million sq. ft.** of space
- **Over 3,000 employees**

Its network spans both countries, with **48 centres in Canada** and **61 in the United States** reported in the 2024 annual report.

## Market Position
Richelieu describes itself as a **leading North American** player in specialty hardware. Its competitive position is built on a **large distribution network, broad product selection, supplier relationships, private-label offerings, and e-commerce capabilities**. The company operates in a **fragmented market** and competes against many regional distributors with narrower assortments.

The company’s growth strategy combines **organic expansion, new distribution centres, and acquisitions**. Investor materials and press releases show this has been a long-running strategy, with the company reaching its **100th acquisition in 2025**.

## History
Richelieu’s modern corporate form dates to **1968**. A major inflection point came in **1988**, when **Richard Lord** became President and CEO; company materials show sales of about **$27 million** at that time. Richelieu went public on the **TSX in 1993**.

From there, the business expanded steadily across Canada and the U.S. through acquisitions and network buildout. This trajectory has established Richelieu as a scaled specialty hardware distributor with manufacturing capabilities and broad North American reach.

## Overview
**Rogers Corporation** is a publicly traded U.S. manufacturer of specialty engineered materials used in high-performance electrical and electronic applications. ## Overview
**Shockwave Medical** is a medical device manufacturer focused on treating **calcified cardiovascular disease** using **Intravascular Lithotripsy (IVL)**. Founded in **2009**, the company is headquartered at **5403 Betsy Ross Drive, Santa Clara, California 95054, USA**. Its core technology adapts lithotripsy principles used for kidney stones to fracture calcium in blood vessels with **sonic pressure waves**, enabling low-pressure balloon dilation and blood-flow restoration.

## Products & Services
- **Shockwave IVL platform** for calcium modification in:
  - **Coronary artery disease (CAD)**
  - **Peripheral artery disease (PAD)**
- Product families include **coronary and peripheral IVL catheters** marketed under the Shockwave brand.
- The company also added the **Reducer System** (via the Neovasc acquisition) for **refractory angina**; it is available in select international markets and investigational in the U.S. and Canada.
- Beyond devices, Shockwave provides:
  - **clinical evidence and physician education**
  - **reimbursement support**
  - **product technical documentation and IFUs**

## Scale
- **2023 revenue:** **$730.2M**
- **Employees:** approximately **1,468-1,500**
- **Headquarters:** Santa Clara, California
- **Locations:** user-provided data indicates **12 locations**
- LinkedIn lists the company in the **1,001-5,000 employee** range.

## Market Position
Shockwave is widely described as a **pioneer** in IVL and, at the time of its acquisition by Johnson & Johnson, was characterized as the **first and only commercially available IVL platform** for both **CAD and PAD**. The company positions IVL as a simpler, minimally invasive alternative for heavily calcified lesions and has emphasized its role in establishing a **new standard of care** for calcium modification in interventional cardiology and peripheral vascular procedures.

The company has also been recognized for innovation, including inclusion in **Fast Company’s 2022 Most Innovative Companies** list in medical devices.

- **2024:** **Johnson & Johnson completed its acquisition** of Shockwave Medical on **May 31, 2024**.

Overall, Shockwave Medical built its reputation around a differentiated calcium-modification platform for interventional cardiovascular care and now operates within the broader global reach of Johnson & Johnson MedTech.

## Overview
**The Manitowoc Company, Inc.** is a U.S.-based **manufacturer of cranes and engineered lifting solutions**. Founded in **1902** in **Manitowoc, Wisconsin**, the company is now headquartered in **Milwaukee, Wisconsin** at **One Park Plaza, 11270 W. Park Place, Suite 1000, Milwaukee, WI 53224**. It is a **public company** traded on the **NYSE under MTW**. Manitowoc describes itself as a global leader in lifting solutions, designing, manufacturing, marketing, distributing, and supporting cranes and related services worldwide.

## Products & Services
Manitowoc’s core business is crane equipment and aftermarket support. Its principal product categories include:
- **Mobile hydraulic cranes**
- **Lattice-boom crawler cranes**
- **Tower cranes**
- **Boom trucks**
- **Carrydeck and industrial cranes**

Key brands include **Grove**, **Manitowoc**, **Potain**, **National Crane**, **Shuttlelift**, **MGX Equipment Services**, and **Upfits by Aspen Equipment**. Beyond equipment sales, the company provides:
- **Parts and accessories**
- **Field service and maintenance**
- **Technical support**
- **Crane rebuilding/remanufacturing**
- **Training**
- **Used equipment, rentals, and digital/telematics-related support**

Its cranes serve end markets such as **infrastructure**, **commercial and residential construction**, **energy and utilities**, **petrochemical**, and **industrial projects**.

## Scale
For **2024**, Manitowoc reported approximately **$2.2 billion in net sales** (company annual report; consistent with provided revenue of **$2,159.8M**). The company employed about **4,800 people** as of year-end 2024 and operates in **more than 20 countries**. The account data provided lists **79 locations**. Manitowoc has a broad global footprint across the **Americas, Europe/Africa, Middle East, and Asia-Pacific**.

## Market Position
Manitowoc is one of the **best-known global crane manufacturers**, with particularly strong recognition in **crawler cranes**, **tower cranes**, and **mobile hydraulic cranes**. Its portfolio spans premium legacy brands, notably **Potain** in tower cranes and **Grove** in mobile cranes. Management has increasingly emphasized higher-margin, less cyclical **aftermarket and non-new machine revenue**—including parts, services, rentals, used cranes, and digital solutions—through its **CRANES+50** strategy.

## History
Manitowoc began as a **shipbuilding and repair company** in 1902. It later diversified into crane manufacturing in the **mid-1920s**, which became a defining part of the business. During **World War II**, the company was a notable builder of **submarines for the U.S. Navy**. Over time it expanded into multiple industrial lines, including refrigeration, before refocusing.

- **1902** – Founded in Manitowoc, Wisconsin
- **Mid-1920s** – Entered crane manufacturing
- **2002** – Acquired **Grove Crane**
- **2016** – Completed the **spin-off of its foodservice equipment business**, becoming a standalone crane-focused company

Today, Manitowoc is a specialized global crane manufacturer with more than **120 years** of industrial history.

## Overview
**Toromont Cat** is a Canadian **Caterpillar equipment dealer and distributor** serving customers across **Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Nunavut**. The company supplies and supports **new and used heavy equipment**, parts, rentals, power systems, and aftermarket service for industries such as construction, mining, aggregates, forestry, paving, waste, marine, and industrial applications.

Toromont Cat was **established in 1993** and operates as a division of **Toromont Industries Ltd. (TSX: TIH)**, a publicly traded Canadian company originally incorporated in **1963**. Its headquarters are in **Vaughan/Concord, Ontario, Canada**.

## Products & Services
- **New equipment:** Cat machines and attachments, with the company citing **300+ machine models**.
- **Used equipment:** Used heavy equipment, used generators, forklifts, attachments, and restored parts.
- **Rentals:** Heavy equipment rentals, generator rentals, and affiliated rental offerings through **Battlefield Equipment Rentals**.
- **Parts & support:** Parts distribution, hoses and hydraulics, undercarriage, ground engaging tools, engine rebuild kits, remanufacturing, and online parts ordering.
- **Service offerings:** Preventive maintenance, diagnostics, fluid analysis, rebuild programs, field service, customer value agreements, and equipment management.
- **Power systems:** Backup and prime power generation systems, rental generators, marine engines, and industrial engines.
- **Technology:** Cat technology, machine control, payload, remote monitoring, and digital fleet/equipment management tools.

## Scale
- **Employees:** Approximately **4,000+** employees; Apollo estimates **4,100**.
- **Locations:** User-provided data indicates **55 locations**; Toromont Cat career materials reference a network of **50 branches** in Canada, while rental materials cite **45 branches** and **1,600+ technicians** plus **350+ service trucks**.
- **Revenue:** User-provided estimate of **$1.4 billion**.
- **Geographic footprint:** One of the largest Cat dealer territories in Canada, spanning **7 provinces and 1 territory**.

## Market Position
Toromont Cat describes itself as **“one of the world’s largest Caterpillar dealers.”** Within Toromont Industries’ Equipment Group, it anchors a broad heavy-equipment platform with strong parts, service, rental, and remanufacturing capabilities. Its market position is strengthened by exclusive Caterpillar dealership rights across a large contiguous Eastern and Central Canadian territory, plus adjacent businesses such as **Battlefield Equipment Rentals**, **SITECH Eastern Canada**, and **Toromont Material Handling**.

## History
- **1993:** Toromont became a Caterpillar dealer through acquisition of the assets of an Ontario dealership (Crothers), creating Toromont Cat.
- **1996:** Awarded the Newfoundland and Labrador Cat franchise; acquired **Battlefield Equipment Rentals**.
- **2001:** Added Cat territories in **Manitoba and Nunavut**.
- **2006:** Added **MaK marine** territory for the Great Lakes region.
- **2017:** Acquired **Hewitt Equipment** and **Atlantic Tractors**, expanding into **Quebec and the Maritimes** and significantly increasing scale.
- **2024:** Announced the acquisition of **Tri-City Equipment**, expanding its heavy equipment rental presence in Southwestern Ontario.

Overall, Toromont Cat has grown from a single Ontario Caterpillar dealership in 1993 into a large, multi-province equipment distribution and support organization with extensive aftermarket and rental capabilities.

## Overview
**TPI Composites, Inc.** is a U.S.-headquartered manufacturer of advanced composite structures, best known as the **largest U.S.-based independent manufacturer of composite wind blades**. The company was **founded in 1968** as **Tillotson Pearson Inc.** and began producing **composite wind blades in 2001**. It is headquartered in **Scottsdale, Arizona**.

TPI focuses on supplying wind turbine original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) through outsourced blade manufacturing, alongside related engineering and field services. The company positions itself around solutions that support **decarbonization and electrification**.

## Products & Services
- **Composite wind blades** manufactured to customer specifications
- **Precision molding and assembly systems** related to blade production
- **Engineering and R&D services** for blade design, manufacturability, materials, and quality
- **Global field services** including inspection, repair, and restoration support for wind blades
- Additional composite capabilities for **transportation and industrial applications**, including vehicle composite structures

TPI states it has manufactured **more than 100,000 wind blades since 2001**.

## Scale
- **2024 net sales:** approximately **$1.3 billion**
- **2024 production:** **6,525 wind blades**
- **Employees/associates:** official company materials cite **over 14,000 associates** globally; third-party sources commonly report around **11,700 employees**
- **Manufacturing footprint:** more than **6 million square feet** of operations
- **Locations:** factories in the **U.S., Mexico, and India**, plus engineering centers in **Denmark** and **Germany** and service training centers in the **U.S., France, United Kingdom, and Spain**

Key manufacturing sites highlighted by the company include **Newton, Iowa; Juarez and Matamoros, Mexico; and Chennai, India**.

## Market Position
TPI is a major supplier in the global wind supply chain and a key outsourcing partner to leading wind turbine OEMs. According to the company, in **2024** it accounted for approximately **27% of all onshore wind blades on a MW basis globally, excluding China**.

The company has historically emphasized a globally distributed manufacturing model located near customer end markets or in cost-advantaged regions to reduce delivered cost and expand OEM capacity.

TPI became a **public company in 2016**, listing on **Nasdaq** under the ticker **TPIC**.

## History
- **1968:** Founded as Tillotson Pearson Inc. in Rhode Island, originally focused on high-performance sail and powerboats and other composite structures
- **1990s–early 2000s:** Shifted strategic focus from marine composites into wind energy
- **2001:** Began producing composite wind blades
- **2008:** Rebranded as **TPI Composites, Inc.**
- **2016:** Completed IPO on Nasdaq
- **2018–2020:** Expanded engineering and manufacturing footprint, including engineering operations in **Denmark** and **Germany** and a manufacturing hub in **Chennai, India**

Overall, TPI Composites has evolved from a legacy composites manufacturer into a large-scale global wind blade specialist with complementary engineering and service capabilities.

**TricorBraun** is a privately held global packaging distributor headquartered in the St. Louis area (Creve Coeur, Missouri). - **Sustainability support**

- **North America’s largest distributor of primary packaging**

## Overview
**Triumph Group** is a U.S.-based **aerospace manufacturer and services provider** headquartered in **Radnor, Pennsylvania**. Founded in **1993**, the company designs, engineers, manufactures, repairs, and overhauls aircraft systems and components for **commercial, regional, military, and business aviation** markets. Triumph’s website describes it as a global aerospace leader with capabilities spanning **design, production, and aftermarket service**. In **2025**, the company agreed to be acquired by **Warburg Pincus** and **Berkshire Partners** in an approximately **$3 billion** take-private transaction.

## Products & Services
Triumph focuses on mission-critical aerospace systems and components, including:
- **Actuation and landing gear systems**
- **Fuel systems** and fuel metering/control products
- **Hydraulics** and hydro-mechanical systems
- **Geared solutions** such as accessory drives and gearboxes
- **Flight controls, cockpit controls, and related assemblies**
- **Interiors, cables, and controls**
- **MRO services** (maintenance, repair, and overhaul) for structures, airframe, engine accessories, and third-party aerospace components

Its customers include major OEMs and operators across the aviation industry, with cited relationships including companies such as **Boeing, Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Gulfstream, Bell, Sikorsky, GE, Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney,** and major commercial and cargo airlines.

## Scale
- **Revenue / net sales:** about **$1.3 billion** (company site / recent profiles)
- **Employees:** approximately **3,800-4,800** globally, depending on source and timing
- **Locations:** **22** locations across **8 countries** (per company overview)
- **HQ phone:** **+1 610-251-1000**

Triumph operates a global footprint across North America and selected international markets, supporting both OEM production and aftermarket demand.

## Market Position
Triumph is positioned as a **specialized aerospace and defense supplier** focused on engineered systems, proprietary components, and aftermarket support rather than complete aircraft manufacturing. The company emphasizes high-value niches such as actuation, landing gear systems, geared solutions, and aerospace MRO. Its market standing has been shaped by a long acquisition history and, more recently, by a portfolio simplification strategy that narrowed focus to higher-margin core aerospace operations.

## History
- **1993:** Formed through a leveraged buyout of businesses divested from **Alco Standard**.
- **1996:** Completed its **IPO** on the NYSE under ticker **TGI**.

- **2025:** Take-private deal announced/completed with **Warburg Pincus** and **Berkshire Partners**; **Jorge L. Valladares III** became **President & CEO**.

Overall, Triumph has evolved from an acquisition-driven roll-up into a more focused aerospace systems and components supplier with a meaningful presence in both OEM and aftermarket channels.

## Overview
**True Value Company** is a U.S.-based **hardlines wholesaler and distributor** serving independently owned hardware and home improvement retailers. The business traces its roots to **1948**, when **John Cotter** founded **Cotter & Company** in Chicago. Its headquarters remain in **Chicago, Illinois** at **8600 W. Bryn Mawr Ave.**

True Value supports a large network of independent retailers with merchandising, distribution, marketing, private-brand programs, manufacturing, and retail support services. The company has described itself as serving **more than 4,500 independently owned stores** across the U.S. and **over 60 countries**.

## Products & Services
True Value distributes a broad assortment of home improvement and hardware products, including:
- **Tools and hardware**
- **Paint and coatings**
- **Plumbing and electrical supplies**
- **Lawn, garden, and outdoor products**
- **Building materials and lumber-related categories**
- **Home maintenance and repair products**

Beyond product distribution, True Value offers retailers:
- **Merchandising and category management**
- **Marketing programs and local advertising**
- **Private-brand products**
- **Store format and remodel support**
- **E-commerce and digital retail support**
- **Training/education programs such as True Value University**
- **Manufacturing**, including a significant paint business

## Scale
- **Estimated revenue:** about **$1.5 billion** (user-provided; consistent with historical reporting of **$1.49 billion in 2017**)
- **Employees:** approximately **3,600** (Apollo estimate); historical public figures have ranged around **2,500-2,800**
- **Locations:** user-provided **13** locations; company also operates through a broad independent retail network rather than company-owned stores
- **Store network served:** **4,500+** independent retailers
- **Geographic reach:** **60+ countries**
- **HQ phone:** **+1 773-695-5000**

## Market Position
True Value is widely recognized as one of the **leading hardlines wholesalers** serving the independent hardware channel. Its brand is longstanding and well known in neighborhood hardware retail. The company’s value proposition centers on helping independent dealers compete with big-box home improvement chains through scale purchasing, distribution, private brands, paint manufacturing, and retail support services.

A notable market differentiator is its combination of **wholesale distribution** with a trusted consumer-facing retail brand used by thousands of locally owned stores.

## History
- **1948:** John Cotter founded **Cotter & Company** with a small group of independent stores.
- **1963:** Cotter acquired **Hibbard, Spencer, Bartlett**, including the **True Value** trademark, whose brand roots date to **1932**.
- **1997:** Cotter & Company merged with ServiStar/Coast to Coast to form **TruServ Corporation**.
- **2005:** The company adopted the **True Value Company** name.
- **2018:** True Value was acquired by **ACON Investments**, ending its long retailer-owned cooperative structure at the corporate level.
- **October 2024:** True Value announced a **Chapter 11 filing** and sale agreement with competitor **Do it Best**.
- **November 22, 2024:** **Do it Best completed the purchase** of True Value’s assets and operations.

Independent True Value stores were not themselves part of the bankruptcy filing and continued operating under the brand.

- **Automation and control** solutions
- **Energy management** and infrastructure modernization services
- **Technology services** including digital infrastructure modernization, cybersecurity, and communications support
- **Project logistics, material management, and supply chain solutions**

## Overview
**VEKA Group** is a privately held, family-owned German manufacturer of PVC (uPVC/PVC-U) profile systems for the building and construction industry. ## Overview
**Vishay Intertechnology, Inc.** is a U.S.-based manufacturer of **discrete semiconductors** and **passive electronic components**. The company was **founded in 1962** by **Dr. Felix Zandman** and is headquartered at **63 Lancaster Avenue, Malvern, Pennsylvania**. Vishay is publicly traded on the **NYSE under the ticker VSH**.

Vishay serves OEMs, EMS providers, and distributors worldwide, supplying components used in **automotive, industrial, computing, consumer, telecommunications, military, aerospace, and medical** applications. The company describes itself as offering **one of the world’s largest portfolios** in its category.

## Products & Services
Vishay’s portfolio spans two broad categories:

- **Discrete semiconductors**
  - MOSFETs
  - Diodes and rectifiers
  - Optoelectronics
  - Selected integrated circuits
  - Sensors and infrared components
- **Passive components**
  - Resistors
  - Capacitors
  - Inductors
  - Custom magnetics

Its products are fundamental building blocks in electronic systems, particularly in **power management, electrification, industrial automation, communications infrastructure, and embedded electronics**.

## Scale

- **Employees:** approximately **22,700** at year-end 2024 (Apollo estimates ~23,000)
- **Locations / manufacturing footprint:** about **60 plants in 19 countries**
- **Geographic presence:** operations across the **Americas, Europe, Asia, and Israel**
- **Market cap:** roughly **$2.5 billion** (Apollo)

## Market Position
Vishay is widely positioned as **one of the world’s largest manufacturers of discrete semiconductors and passive components**. Its broad product catalog and global manufacturing footprint support a diversified role in electronics supply chains.

Recent company messaging highlights growth priorities in **e-mobility, sustainability, smart grid infrastructure, AI server power, aerospace & defense, and healthcare**. Vishay also distinguishes itself through a mix of **commodity, certified, and custom products**.

## History

A major turning point came in **1985**, when Vishay began an acquisition-led expansion to become a broad-line components manufacturer. Key acquisitions over time included **Dale Electronics (1985)**, **Sprague Electric’s tantalum capacitor business (1992)**, **Siliconix (1998)**, and **General Semiconductor (2001)**. This strategy transformed Vishay from a specialist resistor maker into a diversified global electronic components supplier.

More recently, the company has continued reshaping its footprint under its **“Vishay 3.0”** strategy, including manufacturing optimization and investments in higher-growth semiconductor and power electronics markets.

## Overview
**Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions (WMFTS)** is a UK-based manufacturer of **positive displacement pumps** and **associated fluid path technologies**, with a particular focus on **peristaltic pumping** for the **life sciences** and **process industries**. The business traces its origins to **1956**, when founder **Bernard Refson** developed one of the first commercially viable peristaltic pumps for use outside the laboratory in **Marlow, Buckinghamshire**. Its main operational base moved to **Falmouth, Cornwall** in **1969**; corporate office listings cite **Bickland Water Road, Falmouth, TR11 4RU, England**. Since **1990**, WMFTS has been a **wholly owned subsidiary of Spirax Group plc**.

- **Bredel** – heavy-duty hose pumps
- **MasoSine** – sinusoidal/process pumps for gentle handling
- **Watson-Marlow Tubing** – precision tubing, including cleanroom-manufactured and validated options
- **Flexicon** – aseptic liquid filling and capping systems
- **WMArchitect** – single-use solutions
- **BioPure** – fluid path components and connector systems
- **ASEPCO** – high-purity aseptic diaphragm valves
- **Aflex Hose** – PTFE-lined flexible hoses

The company serves sectors including **pharmaceutical and biotechnology, medical and diagnostic devices, food and beverage, water and wastewater, mining, automotive, and OEM markets**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$500.6M** (user-provided)

- **1969:** Operations moved to **Falmouth, Cornwall**
- **1990:** Became part of **Spirax Group plc**

## Overview

- **Drainage & water re-use** systems, including stainless steel and chemical waste drainage
- **HVAC & hot water** products, including hydronic and heating system components
- **Rainwater harvesting** and other water conservation solutions

## Scale
Watts reported approximately **$2.3 billion in 2024 net sales**. Public and third-party sources indicate the company employs about **4,800 people** globally. Investor materials describe a footprint spanning **5 continents** and **36 principal worldwide locations**; the CRM record provided lists **14 locations**. Watts is widely described by the company and outside sources as **one of the world’s leading providers of water technologies and solutions**. Its competitive position is supported by:

- A large installed base that supports **repair and replacement demand**
- Global manufacturing and distribution capabilities
- Active expansion through acquisitions and smart/connected water solutions

Investor materials show revenue exposure weighted toward the **Americas (74%)**, with additional sales in **Europe (20%)** and **APMEA (6%)**.

## History

- **1985:** Watts Water Technologies, Inc. incorporated in Delaware as the parent company

- Over subsequent decades, the company built its business in **foam and plastic foodservice packaging**.
- **2016:** WinCup launched **Vio®**, its biodegradable foam cup technology.
- **2020:** **Atar Capital acquired WinCup** from funds managed by BlackRock; new leadership included **Brad Laporte** as CEO.
- **2020 onward:** WinCup expanded commercialization of **phade®**, which has received industry recognition for biodegradable straw innovation.
- **2023:** the company announced the transition of **all foam products** to **Vio® technology**.
- **2025:** WinCup announced the acquisition of **ConverPack’s paper cup manufacturing capabilities**, expanding hot and cold paper cup production and supporting growth of its phade® cup line.

Overall, WinCup has evolved from a legacy foam packaging manufacturer into a broader foodservice packaging company with a strong emphasis on **sustainability-oriented product development**.

## Overview
**Wolseley Group** is a UK-based **specialist distributor** of plumbing, heating, HVAC, renewables, and infrastructure utility products for trade customers. The business traces its roots to **1887**, while **Wolseley UK Limited** was incorporated on **3 September 1959**. It is headquartered at **2 Kingmaker Court, Warwick Technology Park, Gallows Hill, Warwick, CV34 6DY, United Kingdom**. Since **2021**, the company has been owned by private equity firm **Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R)**.

Wolseley describes itself as a leading specialist merchant serving customers across the **UK and Ireland**, with a large branch network and fulfilment capability.

## Products & Services
Wolseley distributes a broad range of products for professional trade customers, including:
- **Plumbing and heating** supplies
- **Bathrooms** and related fittings
- **Pipe, valves, fittings, drainage, and commercial plumbing** systems
- **Air conditioning, refrigeration, and HVAC** equipment
- **Infrastructure and utility** products
- **Renewables** such as heat pump-related and low-carbon building solutions

Its main trading brands include:
- **Plumb Centre** - over **400 branches**
- **Pipe Centre** - over **40 branches**
- **Climate Centre**
- **William Wilson** in Scotland
- Infrastructure and managed services operations

The company also offers value-added services such as **technical support, training, project support, digital ordering tools, click-and-collect, online tracking, and managed supply-chain services**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$2.94B** provided; latest filed group revenue was **£2.22B in FY2024**
- **Employees:** about **5,775 FTEs** at 31 July 2024; Apollo estimates roughly **6,000 employees**
- **Locations:** around **650 branches** across the **UK and Ireland** (annual report lists **641 branches** at 31 July 2024)
- **Distribution network:** supported by **three major distribution centres**
- **HQ phone:** **01926 705000**

## Market Position
Wolseley is positioned as one of the **largest specialist trade merchants** in the UK plumbing and heating market, and company materials describe it as a leading provider in plumbing, HVAC, and infrastructure distribution. Its competitive strength comes from:
- A dense national branch network
- Specialist brands with category expertise
- Strong fulfilment and logistics capabilities
- Broad product availability and digital trade tools
- Exposure to long-term demand themes such as **repair, maintenance and improvement** and the **energy transition/renewables** market

## History
Key milestones include:
- **1887:** Frederick York Wolseley founded the original **Wolseley Sheep Shearing Machine Company**
- **1958:** Merger with **Geo H Hughes**
- **1960s:** Expansion into UK heating distribution through acquisitions
- **1979:** Strategic repositioning to focus on **distribution**
- **1982:** Acquisition of **Ferguson Enterprises** in the US
- **1985:** Acquisition of **Plumb Center**
- **2017:** Parent company **Wolseley plc** changed name to **Ferguson plc**
- **2021:** **Wolseley UK** was sold by Ferguson to **CD&R**, becoming an independent business
- **2021-2024:** Continued expansion through acquisitions including **Jointing Technologies, Bassetts, DHS, Neville Lumb, Ideal Bathrooms, Cascade Pipeline, Heat Merchants, Hevac, C.P. Hart**, and others

Overall, Wolseley is a long-established distributor that has evolved from industrial origins into a major UK and Ireland trade merchant focused on plumbing, heating, cooling, infrastructure, and renewables.

## Overview
**Woodgrain** is a **private, family-owned manufacturer and distributor of wood building products** serving residential construction, remodeling, and dealer/distributor channels. The company was **founded in 1954** by **Merrill “Bud” Dame** as **Dame Lumber and Moulding Company** in **Cedar City, Utah**. Its corporate headquarters later moved to **Fruitland, Idaho** (in **1969**), where it remains today at **300 NW 16th St, Fruitland, ID 83619**. Main phone: **+1 208-452-3801**.

Woodgrain emphasizes a **vertically integrated model**, controlling much of the supply chain from timber sourcing and sawmilling through remanufacturing, finished products, and distribution.

## Products & Services
Woodgrain manufactures and distributes a broad portfolio of building materials and millwork products, including:
- **Moulding & millwork**: lineal mouldings, decorative mouldings, prefinished and finished mouldings, door and window parts
- **Doors**: interior and exterior wood doors, stile-and-rail doors, door components, pre-hung door fabrication and pre-finishing
- **Windows & patio doors** through **Windsor Windows & Doors**
- **Lumber**: Douglas fir, white fir, ponderosa pine, and hardwood products
- **Engineered/outdoor products** such as **WoodGuard** fencing and engineered lumber
- **Byproduct-based products** including **Nature’s by Woodgrain** animal bedding and **heating pellets**
- **Distribution and logistics services**: fulfillment, 3PL/reload programs, in-store merchandising, and multi-family supply support

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$814.7 million**
- **Employees:** about **2,000** (LinkedIn lists ~**1,955** employees; Apollo estimates **2,000**)
- **Locations:** company materials indicate **over 45 manufacturing and warehouse facilities** across the **United States and Chile**; its distribution network includes **34 warehouses and door shop locations**
- **Geographic footprint:** operations span the U.S. and Chile, with coast-to-coast distribution capabilities

## Market Position
Woodgrain describes itself as **one of the largest millwork operations in the world** and states it is **the largest millwork manufacturer in the United States** on its millwork materials. It is a leading producer of **mouldings, doors, and windows**, and competes in the broader building products and specialty distribution market. Its competitive position is supported by:
- **Vertical integration** from forest to finished goods
- A broad portfolio across millwork, doors, windows, lumber, and specialty building products
- A sizable **distribution platform**, strengthened by the **2022 acquisition of Huttig Building Products**

## History
Key milestones include:
- **1954:** Founded in Utah as **Dame Lumber and Moulding Company**
- **1969:** Corporate offices moved to **Fruitland, Idaho**
- **1973:** Renamed **Woodgrain Millwork Inc.**
- **1985:** Entered doors through acquisition of **Meridian Wood** in Nampa, Idaho
- **1997:** Formed **Woodgrain Chile**
- **1998:** Acquired **Brown Moulding**, helping launch **Woodgrain Distribution**
- **2007:** Acquired **Monarch Windows and Doors**
- **2008:** Started **Nature’s by Woodgrain**
- **2017:** Created **Woodgrain Lumber**
- **2018:** Expanded lumber with acquisition of **two Boise Cascade sawmills**
- **2022:** Distribution division acquired **Huttig Building Products**

Leadership has remained within the Dame family across three generations; **Todd Dame** is identified as **President & CEO**.

## Overview
**Worldwide Oilfield Machine (WOM)** is a **privately held**, vertically integrated manufacturer of oilfield equipment serving the **upstream and midstream oil & gas** markets. The company was **founded in 1980** in **Houston, Texas**, where it remains headquartered at **11809 Canemont Street, Houston, TX 77035**. WOM describes itself as a multinational enterprise focused on pressure and flow-control equipment for **onshore, offshore, and subsea** applications, including **high-pressure/high-temperature (HPHT)** and other extreme-environment use cases.

## Products & Services
WOM designs, manufactures, and services a broad portfolio of oilfield equipment used in **drilling, testing, production, and intervention** operations. Core product categories include:
- **Gate valves** (including the flagship **Magnum Gate Valve**)
- **Ball valves**, block valves, check valves, and control valves
- **Blowout preventers (BOPs)**
- **Wellheads and Christmas trees**
- **Chokes and manifolds** for well testing
- **Subsea equipment** such as subsea wellheads, subsea trees, manifolds, connectors, PLEMs/PLETs, and intervention systems
- **Actuators, control panels, and hydraulic systems**
- **Aftermarket services** including installation, inspection, repair, refurbishment, and field service crews

The company emphasizes vertical integration through in-house forging, casting, engineering, manufacturing, assembly, and testing capabilities.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$814.7M**
- **Employees:** official company materials cite **2,500+ to 3,000+ employees** globally
- **Geographic footprint:** operations in **10 countries**
- **Locations:** manufacturing, engineering, sales, and service sites across the U.S., India, UK, UAE, Singapore, Turkmenistan, South Korea, Australia, and Brazil

Major operating hubs highlighted by the company include **Houston**, **Pune**, **Aberdeen**, **Dubai**, and **Singapore**. WOM India alone reports **1,500+ employees** and substantial manufacturing expansion.

## Market Position
WOM positions itself as a **global supplier of high-pressure flow-control and well-control equipment** and highlights leadership in **HPHT environments**. Its patented **Dual-Seal / Magnum valve technology** is presented as a key differentiator and became an important part of its reputation for reliability and low maintenance. The company serves major oil companies, drilling contractors, and well-testing firms worldwide. WOM also identifies itself as a **minority- and female-owned enterprise**.

## History
Key milestones from company sources include:
- **1980:** Worldwide Oilfield Machine established in Houston, Texas
- **1985:** Patent of the **Magnum Dual-Seal Gate Valve**, a major commercial and technology milestone
- **1986:** Introduction of Magnum gate valves and actuators for drilling and production applications
- **1989:** Establishment of **WOM India** in Pune
- **1997:** Launch of **Magnum Forge**
- **1999:** Establishment of **Magna Casting**
- **2007:** Incorporation of **WOM Asia Pacific** in Singapore
- **2021:** Opening of WOM’s **elastomer plant** for HPHT ram and annular elastomers
- **2023:** Launch of **Magna Specialty Steel**

Overall, WOM has grown from a small Houston repair and aftermarket shop into a large multinational manufacturer with a broad oilfield equipment portfolio and global service network.

## Overview
**WS Audiology (WSA)** is a global **hearing-aid manufacturer** focused on developing, manufacturing, and distributing hearing aids, accessories, and related hearing-care solutions. The company was **formed in 2019** through the merger of **Sivantos** and **Widex**, combining heritage that traces back to **1878**. Its global headquarters is in **Lynge, Denmark** at **Nymøllevej 6, 3540 Lynge**, with a major regional headquarters in **Singapore**. The company positions itself around the mission **“Wonderful Sound for All.”**

## Products & Services
WSA offers a broad portfolio of **hearing aids and hearing-care solutions** across multiple price points and channels.

**Key brands include:**
- **Signia**
- **Widex**
- **Rexton**
- **Audio Service**
- **Vibe**

**Additional channels and service assets cited by the company and market sources include:**
- Wholesale distribution
- Retail hearing-care operations
- Online/direct channels such as **hear.com / audibene**
- Managed care and diagnostic solutions

The company’s portfolio spans premium and value-oriented offerings, including rechargeable and app-connected devices, with ongoing investment in AI-enabled sound processing, fitting tools, and user applications.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** about **€2.63 billion** in FY **2023/24** (roughly aligned with the provided **$2.579B** figure)
- **Employees:** **12,500+ to 13,000** globally
- **Offices:** **45** globally
- **Market presence:** active in **130+ markets** and more than **125 countries**
- **R&D footprint:** **4 dedicated R&D facilities** in **Denmark, Germany, India, and Singapore**
- **Locations:** company materials cite **45 offices globally**

WSA’s Lynge headquarters also serves as a production, distribution, and R&D site employing **1,000+ people**.

## Market Position
WSA is widely described as a **global leader in the hearing-aid industry**. EQT identifies it as the **number one global pure-play producer of hearing aids and accessories by volume**. Reuters and other market sources have described the Sivantos-Widex combination as creating the **world’s No. 3 hearing-aid group** at the time of the merger. The company competes through a **multi-brand strategy**, broad distribution reach, and strong positions in both traditional hearing-care channels and online/direct-to-consumer pathways.

## History
- **1878:** Earliest roots of the business begin through predecessor heritage
- **1956:** Widex founded in Denmark
- **2015:** Siemens’ hearing-aid business, later Sivantos, had been sold by Siemens to EQT and Santo Holding
- **2018:** **Sivantos and Widex announced an $8B merger**
- **2019:** The combined company launched as **WS Audiology**
- **2024:** Company reported **10% organic revenue growth** and **13% EBITDA improvement** for FY 2023/24

WSA today reflects both long-standing audiology heritage and a more recent effort to scale globally through brand consolidation, channel expansion, and continued product innovation.

## Overview
**Würth Industry USA** is a **family-owned, privately held industrial distributor** focused on **fasteners, MRO products, safety supplies, and supply chain solutions**. It operates as part of the **Würth Group**, the German parent company founded in **1945**, and positions itself as a North American arm of the group’s industrial distribution business. The company is headquartered in **Greenwood, Indiana** and lists a main phone number of **+1 877-999-8784**.

Würth Industry emphasizes helping industrial customers manage **C-parts**, inventory, and procurement complexity through local service backed by the purchasing scale and global reach of the Würth Group.

## Products & Services
Würth Industry provides a broad portfolio of industrial products and related services, including:
- **Industrial fasteners** and assembly components
- **MRO supplies**
- **Safety and PPE products**
- **Tools, cleaners, and metalworking-related supplies**
- **Additive manufacturing / 3D printing products and services**

Core service offerings highlighted by the company include:
- **Inventory management**
- **Engineering assistance** for product design and application fit
- **Supply chain solutions**
- **Quality control**
- **Digital Kanban and vending solutions**
- **Kitting and assembly**

Apollo data indicates the company offers **over 420,000 line items**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$369.8M** (user-provided)
- **Employees:** about **570** (Apollo estimate)
- **Locations:** **110** across North America (user-provided; also supported by company materials referencing **110+ locations**)
- **Footprint:** locations across the **U.S., Canada, and Mexico**
- Apollo also describes **50 warehouse stocking locations** and six North American companies within the broader organization.

At the parent level, the **Würth Group** operates **400+ companies** in **80+ countries** and is widely described as the **world market leader** or **world’s largest industrial distributor** in fastening and assembly materials.

## Market Position
Würth Industry competes as a **value-added industrial distributor** rather than only a product reseller. Its differentiation centers on:
- Backing from the global **Würth Group**
- A large North American branch and warehouse network
- Integrated **inventory and supply chain management** capabilities
- Engineering and application support for industrial customers

The company serves sectors such as **manufacturing, construction, transportation, heavy equipment, energy, agriculture, recreation, and military**.

## History
Würth Industry traces its roots to the founding of the **Würth Group in 1945** by **Adolf Würth** in **Künzelsau, Germany** as a wholesale business for screws and nuts. The broader Würth organization grew from a small family business into a global industrial distribution group.

Würth Industry USA describes itself as having started as a **collection of companies with local, regional, and national roots**, later unified into a broader supply chain solutions platform in North America. More recent company materials describe **Würth Industry North America** as a **$1 billion division of the Würth Group**, built around vertical markets including **Industrial, MRO/Safety/Metalworking, Construction, and Specialty Markets**.

## Overview
**Zeon Chemicals L.P.** is a U.S.-based manufacturer of **specialty elastomers, polymers, and specialty chemicals** and a **wholly owned subsidiary of Zeon Corporation** of Tokyo, Japan. The U.S. business was **founded on September 12, 1989**, following Zeon’s acquisition of BF Goodrich Chemicals’ specialty rubber business. It is headquartered in **Louisville, Kentucky** (Bells Lane campus).

The company focuses primarily on the **manufacture and sale of synthetic rubbers** and related high-performance materials used in industrial applications. Zeon positions itself around deep expertise in **C4 and C5 chemistry** and serves markets such as **automotive, industrial, oilfield, electronics, and energy storage**.

## Products & Services
Zeon Chemicals’ portfolio centers on specialty synthetic elastomers and related materials. Publicly cited product families include:
- **Nipol® NBR** (nitrile butadiene rubber)
- **HyTemp® / Nipol ACM** (acrylic rubber)
- **Hydrin® ECO**
- **Zetpol® HNBR** (hydrogenated nitrile rubber)
- **Zeotherm® TPVs**
- **SIS and other non-elastomer products**
- **Li-ion battery materials / rubber-based binders**

These materials are used in products such as **hoses, seals, gaskets, belts, and other performance parts**. The company also provides **technical assistance, SDS/product stewardship resources, and R&D support**.

## Scale
- **Revenue:** approximately **$908.9M** (user-provided / third-party estimate)
- **Employees:** about **470** estimated by Apollo; LinkedIn lists **201-500** employees
- **Founded:** **1989** for Zeon Chemicals L.P.; parent company Zeon Corporation was founded in **1950**
- **Locations:** company materials indicate **4 U.S. locations/facilities**
  - **Louisville, Kentucky** – headquarters / R&D center
  - **Louisville, Kentucky** – Kentucky plant
  - **Hattiesburg, Mississippi** – Mississippi plant
  - **Pasadena, Texas** – Texas site

Zeon Group globally reports **consolidated sales above $2.9B** and more than **3,300 employees** worldwide.

## Market Position
Zeon Chemicals is a significant U.S. specialty rubber producer and is described by parent-company and local business sources as a **world leader in specialty elastomers**. In the U.S., it appears strongest in **specialty synthetic rubber** categories, particularly for demanding sealing and durability applications. Its competitive position is supported by backing from the larger **Zeon Corporation**, a global polymer producer with manufacturing and R&D operations across North America and Asia.

## History
- **1950:** Parent company **Nippon Zeon Co., Ltd.** founded in Japan.
- **October 1989:** Zeon acquired the **specialty rubber business of BF Goodrich Chemicals Co.** in the U.S.
- **September 12, 1989:** **Zeon Chemicals L.P.** established in the United States.
- Over time, the company expanded its U.S. manufacturing footprint to include operations in **Kentucky, Mississippi, and Texas**, while maintaining an **R&D center in Louisville**.
- More recently, Zeon has highlighted growth in **battery materials** and continued investment in advanced specialty materials.

## Overview
**Ziegler CAT** is a **family-owned heavy equipment distributor and service provider** headquartered in the Minneapolis/Bloomington, Minnesota area (**901 W. 94th St., Minneapolis, MN 55420**). Founded in **1914** by **William H. Ziegler** as Wm. H. Ziegler Co. Inc., the company has operated for more than a century and is now one of the larger Caterpillar dealers in the U.S. Official company materials describe it as serving customers across **Minnesota and Iowa**, with broader related operations in agriculture extending into Missouri.

## Products & Services
Ziegler CAT is the **exclusive Cat dealer for Minnesota and Iowa** and sells and services a broad equipment portfolio, including:
- **Cat construction equipment**
- **Paving equipment**
- **Mining equipment**
- **Trucks, generators, and industrial engines**
- **Weiler forestry products**
- **New and used equipment sales**
- **Rental equipment**
- **Parts, repairs, maintenance, and rebuild services**

Across affiliated Ziegler businesses, the company also represents **AGCO**, **Fendt**, **Massey Ferguson**, **Brandt**, and related agricultural equipment brands.

## Scale
Available sources indicate Ziegler CAT operates at substantial regional scale:
- **Revenue:** approximately **$651.8M**
- **Employees:** about **2,100** on the company website; Apollo estimates roughly **2,400**
- **Locations:** **34 locations** in Minnesota and Iowa cited on the company’s About page; the CAT construction/rental business is also described separately as having **25 locations** in those two states
- **HQ phone:** **+1 800-352-2812**

## Market Position
Ziegler CAT positions itself as **one of the largest Cat dealers in North America**. Its long-standing Caterpillar relationship, large branch footprint, and full-service model—covering equipment sales, rental, parts, and field/shop service—support a strong market position in the Upper Midwest. The company serves sectors including **construction, mining, paving, power systems, forestry, trucking, and agriculture**.

## History
Key milestones include:
- **1914:** William H. Ziegler founds the company in Minneapolis
- **1920:** Ziegler becomes distributor for the **C. L. Best Tractor Co.** and sells its first Best 60 tractor
- **1925:** Following the merger of C.L. Best and Holt to form **Caterpillar Tractor Company**, Ziegler is selected as the Caterpillar dealer for Minnesota and the surrounding area
- **1930:** The business had expanded from an **80-square-foot office** to a **50,000-square-foot facility**
- **1987:** Ziegler acquires **Gibbs/Cook Equipment Co.**, expanding its Iowa Caterpillar presence
- **2016:** Opens the **Ziegler Rebuild Center** in Bloomington, Minnesota
- **2023:** **Ziegler Truck Group** is founded

The company’s long history reflects its evolution from an early machinery distributor into a diversified, large-scale regional equipment dealer and service organization.
